352	4. **写一页笔记**，回答三个问题：
353	   - 这个 run 里哪些工作由 open-instruct 包装层完成（配置校验、数据准备、GSM8K 验证器、提交回执）？
354	   - 哪些由 MILES 运行时/Core 适配器完成（SGLang rollout、OLMo-core 训练、权重发布、checkpoint）？
355	   - `[core]` 段的 `reward_final_answer_only`/`reward_reasoning_mode`（[configs/miles/examples/tiny/dev.toml:L71-L77](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/8cd7c9eb4e4d997cd482e9f88f5249d081728d9a/configs/miles/examples/tiny/dev.toml#L71-L77)）最终影响的是哪一层的哪个环节？（提示：判分输入选择，见 [docs/miles/grading.md](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/8cd7c9eb4e4d997cd482e9f88f5249d081728d9a/docs/miles/grading.md)。）
356	5. **验证笔记**：用只读命令抽查你的连线，例如 `ls open_instruct/miles/rewards/`（验证器确实在包装层）、`grep -n "runtime.lock.json" docs/miles/architecture.md`（运行时锁的权威位置）。
357	
358	预期产物：一张三层架构图 + 一页所有权笔记 + 一份 `plan` 输出的对照标注。`plan` 的具体输出本讲未实际执行，**待本地验证**；若 `plan` 因占位路径报提示，记录提示内容并继续——规划本身不需要那些挂载存在。
359	
360	## 6. 本讲小结
361	
362	- **入口唯一**：`python -m open_instruct.miles` 暴露五个子命令 `plan/validate/train/run/status`（另有 `records` 记录分析）；运行时导入延迟到需要的命令，`plan`/`validate` 无 GPU、无 MILES 运行时即可运行。
363	- **结构化双轨**：含 `schema_version` 或 `model` 的 TOML 编译为 RunSpec（`run`/`status` 只接受这种）；低层 RunConfig 仅供 `plan`/`validate`/`train`。
364	- **三层所有权**：open-instruct 包装层管配置/数据/奖励/提交；MILES 运行时管 rollout 编排与共享 RL 机制；Core 适配器经 OLMo-core 训练、SGLang 服务。后端不导入 open-instruct，open-instruct 以回调与可信注册表注入能力。
365	- **不弃用旧路线**：`grpo.py` 与 `grpo_fast.py` 仍是稠密模型与历史复现的现行选择；MILES 面向受支持的 Olmo MoE 模型。
366	- **文档地图本轮扩展**：`grading.md`（共享判分输入，PR #2250）与 `abstention.md`（Nemotron 弃答 QA，PR #2255 之外由 #2252 引入）经上下文链接与 mkdocs 导航接入；首页表格是精选而非穷举。
367	- **示例按模型家族重组**：`configs/miles/examples/tiny/`（dev/node/three-node）与 `small/`（暂为 tiny dev 的副本占位），grpo.md 与 architecture.md 中的路径已同步更新。
368	
369	## 7. 下一步学习建议
370	
371	下一讲 **u8-l2（配置系统：TOML → RunSpec → RunConfig）** 将拆开本讲只碰了一下的编译链：`configuration/run_spec.py` 的加载与编译、CoreConfig/RunConfig 如何编译出参数列表并挂接奖励/数据钩子、constraints 驱动的校验，以及本轮新增的判分与 score-centering 编译选项。
372	
373	在进入下一讲之前，建议先做两件源码阅读：
374	
375	1. 浏览 `open_instruct/miles/configuration/` 目录（`ls` 即可），对照 [docs/miles/architecture.md:L276-L291](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/8cd7c9eb4e4d997cd482e9f88f5249d081728d9a/docs/miles/architecture.md#L276-L291) 的职责表建立印象。
376	2. 通读 [docs/miles/workflow.md](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/8cd7c9eb4e4d997cd482e9f88f5249d081728d9a/docs/miles/workflow.md)（配合 u8-l3），了解一次 run 从准备、训练到导出的阶段划分，为后续所有 MILES 讲义提供骨架。
377	
378	若想先横向扩展，可回看 u6-l4（`grpo_fast.py` 的 Ray 拓扑）对比两条 RL 路线的架构差异。

# u8-l1 MILES 总览与架构分层

## 1. 本讲目标

学完本讲，你应该能够：

1. 说出 MILES 与 `grpo.py`（Core/vLLM）、`grpo_fast.py`（DeepSpeed/vLLM）三条 RL 训练路线的关系与各自适用范围。
2. 理解 MILES 的所有权分层：open-instruct 包装层负责什么、MILES 运行时负责什么、Core 适配器经 OLMo-core 与 SGLang 又负责什么。
3. 会用 `python -m open_instruct.miles` 的五个子命令（`plan` / `validate` / `train` / `run` / `status`）以及 `records` 记录分析工具。
4. 知道维护示例已按模型家族重组：`configs/miles/examples/tiny/` 与 `configs/miles/examples/small/`，并了解本轮文档地图的扩展（`grading.md`、`abstention.md`）。

本讲是 MILES 单元（u8）的第一篇，只做总览不深入细节；配置系统、工作流执行、奖励体系分别在 u8-l2、u8-l3、u8-l6 及之后各讲展开。

## 2. 前置知识

阅读本讲前，建议先具备以下概念（不熟悉也没关系，下面用通俗语言解释）：

- **RLVR / GRPO**：可验证奖励强化学习（RL with Verifiable Rewards）。对数学题、代码这类有标准答案的任务，可以用一个「验证器」自动判分作为奖励，而不需要训练额外的奖励模型。GRPO 是一种组相对策略优化算法：对同一个 prompt 采样一组回答，按组内奖励的相对高低计算优势。已在 u6-l1、u6-l2 讲过。
- **rollout（ rollout 编排）**：RL 训练的一步是「让当前策略生成一批回答 → 判分 → 用结果更新策略」。生成这批回答的过程及其调度（队列、准入、引擎管理）称为 rollout 编排。
- **Ray actor**：Ray 分布式框架中的常驻进程，持有 GPU 资源并响应远程调用。MILES 运行时用 Ray actor 承载训练器与推理引擎。
- **OLMo-core 与 SGLang**：OLMo-core 是 Allen AI 的模型与分布式训练库（提供模型结构、checkpoint、分布式原语）；SGLang 是推理服务框架。MILES 用前者训练、后者服务。
- **TOML run 文件**：MILES 用一个结构化 TOML 文件描述一次完整运行（模型、数据、拓扑、启动、追踪等），是所有子命令的输入。
- **Beaker**：AI2 的实验平台，MILES 的 `run` 子命令把 TOML 编译成 Beaker 实验提交。不熟悉 Beaker 也不影响本讲，详见 u8-l8。

## 3. 本讲源码地图

| 文件 | 作用 |
|---|---|
| [docs/miles/index.md](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/8cd7c9eb4e4d997cd482e9f88f5249d081728d9a/docs/miles/index.md) | MILES 文档首页：定位声明、入门顺序、文档地图表、权威性与维护规则 |
| [docs/miles/architecture.md](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/8cd7c9eb4e4d997cd482e9f88f5249d081728d9a/docs/miles/architecture.md) | 架构与开发：分层所有权表、运行时锁与镜像、启动依赖、本地开发检查、适配器包布局 |
| [open_instruct/miles/__main__.py](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/8cd7c9eb4e4d997cd482e9f88f5249d081728d9a/open_instruct/miles/__main__.py) | CLI 入口：`python -m open_instruct.miles`，加载 run 文件并分发 plan/validate/train/run/status 与 records |
| [docs/miles/grpo.md](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/8cd7c9eb4e4d997cd482e9f88f5249d081728d9a/docs/miles/grpo.md) | MILES GRPO 指南：首次运行步骤、配置约定、判分/截断/未判分语义、发布模式 |
| [configs/miles/examples/README.md](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/8cd7c9eb4e4d997cd482e9f88f5249d081728d9a/configs/miles/examples/README.md) | 维护示例的导读：按模型家族分组（tiny/small），列出各模板用途与基线设置 |
| [configs/miles/examples/tiny/dev.toml](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/8cd7c9eb4e4d997cd482e9f88f5249d081728d9a/configs/miles/examples/tiny/dev.toml) | 单 GPU 共置（colocated）微型模型力学检查模板，本讲实践对象 |
| [docs/miles/grading.md](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/8cd7c9eb4e4d997cd482e9f88f5249d081728d9a/docs/miles/grading.md) | 本轮新增：共享判分输入（ResponseParts、objective/scope/require_response 契约）与行为变更登记 |
| [docs/miles/abstention.md](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/8cd7c9eb4e4d997cd482e9f88f5249d081728d9a/docs/miles/abstention.md) | 本轮新增：Nemotron 弃答式 QA 奖励的语义、rubric 与裁判服务复用 |

## 4. 核心概念与源码讲解

### 4.1 CLI 入口：`python -m open_instruct.miles`

#### 4.1.1 概念说明

MILES 在 open-instruct 中的公开入口只有一条命令：`python -m open_instruct.miles`。它把「规划、校验、本地执行、Beaker 提交、状态查询」以及「推理记录分析」全部收拢到一个入口后面。

为什么这样设计？

- **研究者的全部意图浓缩在一个 TOML run 文件里**。同一条命令对不同子命令复用同一份配置，避免「训练用一套脚本、提交用另一套脚本」的漂移。
- **运行时导入是延迟的**。GPU/MILES 运行时只在真正需要的子命令里才 import，因此 `plan` / `validate` 这类规划命令在没有 GPU、没有安装 MILES 私有运行时的笔记本电脑上也能运行。这一点是文档明确承诺的：[docs/miles/index.md:L21-L23](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/8cd7c9eb4e4d997cd482e9f88f5249d081728d9a/docs/miles/index.md#L21-L23) 写明 "Planning does not require GPUs or mounted checkpoints"。

#### 4.1.2 核心流程

CLI 的一次执行流程：

```text
python -m open_instruct.miles COMMAND CONFIG.toml [--set SECTION.KEY=VALUE ...]
        │
        ├─ sys.argv[1] == "records"？
        │    ├─ "select"        → open_instruct.miles.datasets.record_selection
        │    ├─ "replay-pool"   → open_instruct.miles.datasets.replay_summary
        │    └─ 其他            → miles.utils.record_summary（需 MILES 运行时）
        │
        └─ 否则：argparse 解析 COMMAND ∈ {plan, validate, train, run, status}
             │
             ├─ 读取 TOML → payload
             ├─ 判断结构化：payload 含 schema_version 或 model 字段？
             │    ├─ 是 → specs.from_dict(...) 解析为 RunSpec（结构化 run 文件）
             │    └─ 否 → RunConfig.from_dict(...)（低层原始配置）
             │
             └─ 按命令分发：
                  plan     → config.plan()，打印计划 JSON + 提示（advisories）
                  validate → 结构化：plan() 全量校验；原始：parse_runtime()
                  run      → execution.launch.run()（提交 Beaker，仅限结构化）
                  status   → execution.launch.status()（仅限结构化）
                  train    → workflow.execute(config)（结构化）/ train_config（原始）
                             （OPDRunSpec 走独立的 distillation.opd_runtime 路径）
```

注意两个设计点：

1. **结构化 run 文件与低层配置双轨**。`run`/`status` 只接受 `schema_version=1` 的结构化文件；低层原始配置只支持 `plan`/`validate`/`train`。这让「研究者视角的完整 run」与「底层调参视角的 CoreConfig」都能进门，但提交必须走结构化路线。
2. **错误处理友好**。输入错误（`InputError`）默认被转成一行 `parser.error` 提示而不是一长串 traceback，加 `--debug` 才展开。

#### 4.1.3 源码精读

模块 docstring 即是命令速查，明确写出五个子命令与 records 的用法：[open_instruct/miles/__main__.py:L1-L12](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/8cd7c9eb4e4d997cd482e9f88f5249d081728d9a/open_instruct/miles/__main__.py#L1-L12)。其中 L4-L5 说明「运行时导入延迟到需要它的命令，规划无需 GPU 栈」这一关键约束。

`main()` 的第一步先拦截 `records` 分支，按子命令名选择实现模块；若缺 `miles` 包则给出「需在锁定运行时中运行」的退出提示：[open_instruct/miles/__main__.py:L26-L44](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/8cd7c9eb4e4d997cd482e9f88f5249d081728d9a/open_instruct/miles/__main__.py#L26-L44)。这段代码同时示范了「延迟导入」模式——`importlib.import_module` 只在确定目标后才执行。

主解析器只有三个位置：命令、配置路径与可重复的 `--set` 覆盖：[open_instruct/miles/__main__.py:L45-L57](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/8cd7c9eb4e4d997cd482e9f88f5249d081728d9a/open_instruct/miles/__main__.py#L45-L57)。L46 的 `choices=("plan", "validate", "train", "run", "status")` 就是「五个子命令」的出处。

`execute()` 读取 TOML 文档后，用 `schema_version in payload or "model" in payload` 判定结构化与否，再分别构造 `RunSpec`（经 `specs.from_dict`）或 `RunConfig`：[open_instruct/miles/__main__.py:L66-L73](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/8cd7c9eb4e4d997cd482e9f88f5249d081728d9a/open_instruct/miles/__main__.py#L66-L73)。这是「TOML → RunSpec → RunConfig」编译链的入口（编译链细节在 u8-l2 精读）。

`plan` 分支调用 `config.plan()` 并打印 JSON 与 advisories，不做任何 GPU 操作：[open_instruct/miles/__main__.py:L74-L78](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/8cd7c9eb4e4d997cd482e9f88f5249d081728d9a/open_instruct/miles/__main__.py#L74-L78)。

`run`/`status` 要求结构化文件并延迟导入 `execution.launch`：[open_instruct/miles/__main__.py:L79-L87](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/8cd7c9eb4e4d997cd482e9f88f5249d081728d9a/open_instruct/miles/__main__.py#L79-L87)。L81 的报错信息直接写明「raw configs support plan/validate/train」。

`validate` 与 `train` 的分发：结构化校验会连物理分配一起 `plan()`，而训练交给 `workflow.execute`（细节在 u8-l3）：[open_instruct/miles/__main__.py:L96-L109](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/8cd7c9eb4e4d997cd482e9f88f5249d081728d9a/open_instruct/miles/__main__.py#L96-L109)。OPD（蒸馏）规格有独立分支（L88-L95），本讲不展开。

#### 4.1.5 小练习与答案

**练习 1**：为什么 `run`/`status` 拒绝低层原始配置（`RunConfig`），只接受 `schema_version=1` 的结构化文件？

**参考答案**：`run` 要把「模型、数据、拓扑、启动、挂载」完整编译成 Beaker 实验，这些信息只有结构化 RunSpec 才齐备；低层 `RunConfig` 只描述训练器参数，缺少提交所需的 launch/output 等段落。源码在 [open_instruct/miles/__main__.py:L79-L81](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/8cd7c9eb4e4d997cd482e9f88f5249d081728d9a/open_instruct/miles/__main__.py#L79-L81) 显式报错。

**练习 2**：`python -m open_instruct.miles records summarize` 与 `plan` 对运行环境的依赖有何不同？

**参考答案**：`records summarize` 分发到 MILES 包内的 `miles.utils.record_summary`，需要安装 MILES 私有运行时（缺失时报「requires the MILES package」）；`plan` 只依赖 open-instruct 的 CPU 配置代码，无需 GPU 栈。见 [open_instruct/miles/__main__.py:L27-L44](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/8cd7c9eb4e4d997cd482e9f88f5249d081728d9a/open_instruct/miles/__main__.py#L27-L44)。

**练习 3**：`--set name=my-run` 这样的覆盖发生在哪个阶段？与直接改 TOML 有何区别？

**参考答案**：覆盖作为 `overrides` 参数传给 `specs.from_dict` / `RunConfig.from_dict`（[open_instruct/miles/__main__.py:L69-L73](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/8cd7c9eb4e4d997cd482e9f88f5249d081728d9a/open_instruct/miles/__main__.py#L69-L73)），在解析时叠加到 TOML 文档之上。区别：TOML 文件保持原样（可继续作为版本化的基准），覆盖只影响这一次调用，适合临时调参、sweep 与调试。

### 4.2 架构分层：三层所有权与适配器包布局

#### 4.2.1 概念说明

MILES 不是「又一个训练脚本」，而是把一次 RL 运行拆给三个所有者：

- **open-instruct 包装层**：研究者面对的一切——配置校验、数据准备、验证器/奖励、Beaker 提交与回执、运行产物。
- **MILES 运行时**（私有、按锁定制）：rollout actor、SGLang 推理引擎、采样/优势/损失机制、共享传输。
- **Core 适配器**（位于 MILES 内）：模型构建、打分与训练前向、梯度同步、优化器与 checkpoint、权重导出；训练走 OLMo-core，服务走 SGLang。

为什么要有这条边界？因为 open-instruct 是公开研究仓库，而 MILES 运行时（含其 pinned fork）是独立发布的私有组件。open-instruct 负责「研究者想要什么」，MILES 负责「RL 机制怎么做」，Core 适配器负责「在 OLMo-core 上真正训练」。理解这条边界后，你在 open-instruct 仓库里看到的每个 `open_instruct/miles/` 子包都能归位到某一层。

同时要记住：**MILES 不取代既有 GRPO 训练器**。`grpo.py`（Core/vLLM）与 `grpo_fast.py`（DeepSpeed/vLLM，u6-l4 讲过其 Ray 拓扑）仍是稠密模型训练与历史复现的现行选择；MILES 面向受支持的 Olmo MoE 模型（也提供稠密 Olmo 3 适配器，但验证较少）。

#### 4.2.2 核心流程

一次 MILES 运行的纵向视角：

```text
研究者编写 run.toml（schema_version=1）
        │  python -m open_instruct.miles plan / validate      ← open-instruct：CPU 校验与规划
        ▼
RunSpec ──编译──▶ RunConfig（含 CoreConfig 与原生 MILES 选项）
        │  python -m open_instruct.miles run                  ← open-instruct：编译 Beaker 实验并提交
        ▼
Beaker 上的应用镜像（按 runtime/miles/runtime.lock.json 构建）
        │
        ▼
MILES 运行时启动：Ray 集群、裁判加载、工作流准备并发启动
        │
        ▼
Core 适配器（OLMoCoreTrainRayActor）：SGLang 服务策略 → rollout → 打分 →
OLMo-core 训练前向/反向 → 权重发布（refresh/barrier/engine_drain）→ checkpoint/导出
```

分层所有权表（五层，前三层是所有权划分，后两层是上游基座）：

| 层 | 拥有 |
|---|---|
| Open Instruct 包装层 | 配置校验、准备、验证器、提交/回执、运行产物 |
| MILES 运行时 | rollout actor、SGLang 引擎、采样/优势/损失机制、共享传输助手 |
| Core 适配器（在 MILES 中） | 模型构建、文档/回放对齐、打分与训练前向、梯度同步、优化器/checkpoint、张量导出 |
| OLMo-core | 模型与分布式训练原语、注意力/专家执行 |
| olmo-sglang | 服务架构注册与模型专属执行 |

#### 4.2.3 源码精读

定位声明与三句式所有权划分写在文档首页开头：[docs/miles/index.md:L3-L6](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/8cd7c9eb4e4d997cd482e9f88f5249d081728d9a/docs/miles/index.md#L3-L6) ——「Open Instruct owns the researcher configuration and data/reward integration; MILES owns rollout orchestration and shared RL machinery; the adapter trains through OLMo-core and serves through SGLang」。

与既有训练器的关系（不弃用、仍可用、按模型与负载选择）：[docs/miles/index.md:L8-L13](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/8cd7c9eb4e4d997cd482e9f88f5249d081728d9a/docs/miles/index.md#L8-L13)。GRPO 指南开头同样强调「recommended path for supported Olmo MoE models…Existing Core/vLLM and DeepSpeed/vLLM workflows remain available」：[docs/miles/grpo.md:L3-L8](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/8cd7c9eb4e4d997cd482e9f88f5249d081728d9a/docs/miles/grpo.md#L3-L8)。

架构页第一段给出「RunSpec 编译成 RunConfig（含 CoreConfig 与原生 MILES 选项）」的链条，并指出 Python API 也可供集成使用：[docs/miles/architecture.md:L3-L6](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/8cd7c9eb4e4d997cd482e9f88f5249d081728d9a/docs/miles/architecture.md#L3-L6)。

上文的五层所有权表出自：[docs/miles/architecture.md:L8-L14](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/8cd7c9eb4e4d997cd482e9f88f5249d081728d9a/docs/miles/architecture.md#L8-L14)。Core 训练 actor 的边界（`miles.backends.core_utils.actor.OLMoCoreTrainRayActor` 实现训练边界，模型/checkpoint 代码住在 pinned MILES fork 中）见：[docs/miles/architecture.md:L16-L21](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/8cd7c9eb4e4d997cd482e9f88f5249d081728d9a/docs/miles/architecture.md#L16-L21)。

运行时依赖的「事实源」是 `runtime/miles/runtime.lock.json`——锁定依赖 commit 与不可变二进制基座，构建时不打补丁、不跟随分支尖端；open-instruct 自身的普通环境保持独立版本：[docs/miles/architecture.md:L25-L30](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/8cd7c9eb4e4d997cd482e9f88f5249d081728d9a/docs/miles/architecture.md#L25-L30)。这就是「MILES 训练镜像 ≠ open-instruct 开发环境」的原因（对启动与镜像的影响见 u8-l8）。

open-instruct 侧的代码按职责分包，`configuration`/`execution` 等八个包与 MILES 侧 `backends/core_utils` 的分工表在：[docs/miles/architecture.md:L271-L298](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/8cd7c9eb4e4d997cd482e9f88f5249d081728d9a/docs/miles/architecture.md#L271-L298)。L288-L291 特别澄清了三个容易混淆的数据模块：MILES `backends/core_utils/data.py` 适配样本给训练器；`rollout/data_source.py` 拥有运行时数据源行为；`datasets/run_data.py` 准备研究者输入。

后端训练器与托管 rollout 模块**不导入 open-instruct**；open-instruct 以回调形式供给 `core_records_factory`（逐题记录）与 `core_evaluation_snapshot`（按需 HF 导出）：[docs/miles/architecture.md:L304-L318](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/8cd7c9eb4e4d997cd482e9f88f5249d081728d9a/docs/miles/architecture.md#L304-L318)。这是三层边界的代码级体现：依赖箭头从 MILES 指向接口，而不是反过来。

#### 4.2.5 小练习与答案

**练习 1**：MILES 与 `grpo_fast.py` 都用 Ray + 多进程做 RL，本质区别是什么？

**参考答案**：`grpo_fast.py` 是 open-instruct 仓库内的一个完整训练脚本（DeepSpeed 训练器 + vLLM 引擎，代码全部在本仓库，u6-l4）；MILES 把「rollout 编排与共享 RL 机制」交给私有 MILES 运行时（按 `runtime.lock.json` 锁定），open-instruct 只保留配置/数据/奖励集成与提交，训练走 OLMo-core、服务走 SGLang。另见 [docs/miles/index.md:L8-L13](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/8cd7c9eb4e4d997cd482e9f88f5249d081728d9a/docs/miles/index.md#L8-L13)：引入 MILES 不弃用既有 GRPO 训练器。

**练习 2**：如果要在 MILES 训练中新增一种自定义验证器，改动应落在哪一层？为什么？

**参考答案**：落在 open-instruct 包装层的 `open_instruct/miles/rewards/`（验证器、奖励路由与托管裁判），以可信注册表条目（factory + 配置）暴露给 MILES。因为后端训练器与托管 rollout 模块不导入 open-instruct（[docs/miles/architecture.md:L304-L313](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/8cd7c9eb4e4d997cd482e9f88f5249d081728d9a/docs/miles/architecture.md#L304-L313)），MILES 侧只通过约定路径消费应用侧回调与注册表。（验证器细节见 u8-l6。）

**练习 3**：为什么 open-instruct 的普通 `uv.lock` 环境跑不了 MILES 训练，而 `plan` 却能跑？

**参考答案**：训练需要 MILES 私有运行时、SGLang 与锁定版本的 OLMo-core，这些由 `runtime/miles/runtime.lock.json` 与专用应用镜像提供（[docs/miles/architecture.md:L25-L30](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/8cd7c9eb4e4d997cd482e9f88f5249d081728d9a/docs/miles/architecture.md#L25-L30)、[docs/miles/architecture.md:L179-L193](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/8cd7c9eb4e4d997cd482e9f88f5249d081728d9a/docs/miles/architecture.md#L179-L193)）；`plan` 只走 CPU 配置代码，CLI 把运行时 import 延迟到需要它的命令（[open_instruct/miles/__main__.py:L4-L5](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/8cd7c9eb4e4d997cd482e9f88f5249d081728d9a/open_instruct/miles/__main__.py#L4-L5)）。

### 4.3 文档地图与本轮扩展

#### 4.3.1 概念说明

`docs/miles/` 是 MILES 的权威文档目录：当前指令都住在这里，示例 TOML 表达起始配方，配置代码 + pinned 原生解析器快照 + `runtime/miles/runtime.lock.json` 共同定义「接受哪些设置、运行时来源是什么」。理解文档地图的意义在于：MILES 的文档是**分层且部分自动生成**的——四个参考页由 MkDocs 从配置源在内存中生成、不入库，手写文档与生成文档的维护方式不同。

本轮（bae4209 → 8cd7c9eb，五个提交）文档地图的扩展主要有两处，都与本单元后续讲义直接相关：

1. **`docs/miles/grading.md`（共享判分输入）**：PR #2250 统一了 MILES 的判分输入——历史上各判分器自己选答案区域，思考里的正确答案可能拿到分而交付答案却是错的；现在由共享的 `ResponseParts` 一次切分 thinking 与交付响应，并用 objective（answer/process/format/composite）× scope × require_response 声明每个验证器的输入契约。GRPO 指南的「Final-answer-only rewards」一节相应改写并链接该页（深入讲解在 u8-l12）。
2. **`docs/miles/abstention.md`（Nemotron 弃答 QA）**：PR #2252 新增原生弃答式 QA 奖励链路：`nemo_abstention_v1` 源适配器 + 从 NVIDIA-NeMo/Gym 移植的 rubric + 复用既有裁判服务（深入讲解在 u8-l13）。

同时，PR #2255 把维护示例按**模型家族**重组为 `tiny/` 与 `small/` 两个目录，GRPO 指南与架构页中的所有示例路径随之更新。

#### 4.3.2 核心流程

文档地图的检索路径：

```text
docs/miles/index.md（首页）
  ├─ Start here 五步入门顺序（L15-L23）
  ├─ Documentation map 表：按「什么时候用」组织的主表（L27-L53）
  └─ Authority and maintenance：权威性与生成式文档的维护规则（L55-L66）

mkdocs.yml 导航（/miles/ 一节）
  └─ 站点导航比首页表格更全：grading.md 在 "Data and rewards" 下（L120）

正文中的上下文链接
  ├─ grpo.md → grading.md（判分契约，L107/L177）
  └─ source-preparation.md → abstention.md（弃答 QA，L578）
```

要点：**首页文档表不是穷举**。`grading.md`、`abstention.md` 等新页通过站点导航与上下文链接接入，而不是（尚）作为首页表格的行出现。查文档时要两条路径都走。

维护规则方面，自动生成参考页用 `python -m scripts.miles.generate_docs` 生成、`--check` 校验；普通文档构建与本地 `plan`/`validate` 都不需要安装 MILES：[docs/miles/index.md:L55-L66](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/8cd7c9eb4e4d997cd482e9f88f5249d081728d9a/docs/miles/index.md#L55-L66)。

#### 4.3.3 源码精读

入门五步顺序（从 GRPO 指南开始，到复制结构化示例、读 workflow、follow 启动指南、用 operations 判完成）：[docs/miles/index.md:L15-L23](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/8cd7c9eb4e4d997cd482e9f88f5249d081728d9a/docs/miles/index.md#L15-L23)。注意 L20 已经指向按家族重组后的示例目录（`configs/miles/examples/README.md`）。

首页的文档地图主表（「Document | Use it when」两列，共 25 行）：[docs/miles/index.md:L25-L53](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/8cd7c9eb4e4d997cd482e9f88f5249d081728d9a/docs/miles/index.md#L25-L53)。这张表本身没有 grading.md/abstention.md 的行——两页经由下面的链接接入。

GRPO 指南「Truncated responses」一节末尾引出判分契约文档：截断零奖励的基线不可与其他奖励后处理组合，「最终答案选择与显式验证器例外见 grading.md」：[docs/miles/grpo.md:L96-L107](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/8cd7c9eb4e4d997cd482e9f88f5249d081728d9a/docs/miles/grpo.md#L96-L107)。

本轮改写后的「Final-answer-only rewards」一节：`core.reward_final_answer_only=true` 只判最后一个字面 `</think>` 之后的文本；缺失闭合标记、空白最终答案或重开思考会拿到「要求响应的验证器的地板分」而不调用它；共享 `ResponseParts` 区分 thinking 与交付的答案/动作，可信注册表声明用 objective 标识 answer/process/format/composite：[docs/miles/grpo.md:L161-L177](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/8cd7c9eb4e4d997cd482e9f88f5249d081728d9a/docs/miles/grpo.md#L161-L177)。这一节是 u8-l12 的门牌。

验证器的消费者迁移契约（可选实现 `async_call_final_answer`、迁移消费者收到 `selected_input=True` 并跳过自己的思考边界逻辑、结构化消费者可用 `async_call_parts`）：[docs/miles/grpo.md:L179-L189](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/8cd7c9eb4e4d997cd482e9f88f5249d081728d9a/docs/miles/grpo.md#L179-L189)。

`docs/miles/grading.md` 自身开门见山给出动机——「历史上各判分器自选答案区域，思考里的正确答案可能得分而交付答案错误或未完成」——并声明该页登记相对基线 commit 的有效判分变更：[docs/miles/grading.md:L1-L4](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/8cd7c9eb4e4d997cd482e9f88f5249d081728d9a/docs/miles/grading.md#L1-L4)。

弃答 QA 文档（经 source-preparation 链接接入）：`nemo_abstention_v1` 源适配器保留原始 system/user 消息并输出结构化 question/reference 目标，训练需命名裁判，纯答案匹配无法复现弃答目标：[docs/miles/abstention.md:L1-L4](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/8cd7c9eb4e4d997cd482e9f88f5249d081728d9a/docs/miles/abstention.md#L1-L4)；接入点在 [docs/miles/source-preparation.md:L578](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/8cd7c9eb4e4d997cd482e9f88f5249d081728d9a/docs/miles/source-preparation.md#L578)。

站点导航中 grading.md 的条目（"Grading inputs and changes"，位于 Data and rewards 组）：[mkdocs.yml:L118-L124](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/8cd7c9eb4e4d997cd482e9f88f5249d081728d9a/mkdocs.yml#L118-L124)。

维护示例的模型家族重组：`tiny/` 收纳既有配方（dev/node/three-node），`small/` 目前只有复制自 tiny dev 的起始文件，为 upcoming 的模型/拓扑工作预留：[configs/miles/examples/README.md:L1-L15](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/8cd7c9eb4e4d997cd482e9f88f5249d081728d9a/configs/miles/examples/README.md#L1-L15)。

示例基线声明（除非明确声明否则以示例为准，尤其保持 `miles.calculate_per_token_loss=false`、`core.reward_zero_truncated=true`、`core.reward_final_answer_only=true` 与 `core.reward_reasoning_mode="required"`；process/boundary-format 奖励需声明例外，见 grading 契约）：[configs/miles/examples/README.md:L21-L32](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/8cd7c9eb4e4d997cd482e9f88f5249d081728d9a/configs/miles/examples/README.md#L21-L32)。

#### 4.3.5 小练习与答案

**练习 1**：想在本地修改 `docs/miles/configuration.md` 中的一个字段默认值，直接编辑该文件对吗？

**参考答案**：不对。`configuration.md` 等四个参考页由 MkDocs 从配置源在内存中生成、不入库；应编辑源定义与审校描述，再用 `python -m scripts.miles.generate_docs` 重新生成、`--check` 校验。见 [docs/miles/index.md:L55-L63](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/8cd7c9eb4e4d997cd482e9f88f5249d081728d9a/docs/miles/index.md#L55-L63)。

**练习 2**：`tiny/dev.toml` 与 `small/dev.toml` 目前内容几乎相同，为什么还要分两个目录？

**参考答案**：示例按**模型家族**重组——`tiny/` 收纳现有的微型模型配方（单 GPU 力学检查、单节点、三节点），`small/` 为即将开展的更大模型/拓扑工作提供起始文件占位。README 明说 small 的 dev「does not qualify a larger model on the one-GPU smoke-test layout」：[configs/miles/examples/README.md:L13-L15](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/8cd7c9eb4e4d997cd482e9f88f5249d081728d9a/configs/miles/examples/README.md#L13-L15)。

**练习 3**：`core.reward_final_answer_only` 的库默认值与维护示例值分别是什么？为什么示例要显式写出？

**参考答案**：库默认 `false`（保留历史判分行为），维护示例显式设 `true`（思考型策略只判交付响应）。示例是配置基线——除非 run 明确声明，应以示例为准，显式写出避免「沉默改变目标」。见 [docs/miles/grading.md:L7-L12](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/8cd7c9eb4e4d997cd482e9f88f5249d081728d9a/docs/miles/grading.md#L7-L12) 与 [configs/miles/examples/tiny/dev.toml:L71-L77](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/8cd7c9eb4e4d997cd482e9f88f5249d081728d9a/configs/miles/examples/tiny/dev.toml#L71-L77)。

## 6. 本讲小结

- **入口唯一**：`python -m open_instruct.miles` 暴露五个子命令 `plan/validate/train/run/status`（另有 `records` 记录分析）；运行时导入延迟到需要的命令，`plan`/`validate` 无 GPU、无 MILES 运行时即可运行。
- **结构化双轨**：含 `schema_version` 或 `model` 的 TOML 编译为 RunSpec（`run`/`status` 只接受这种）；低层 RunConfig 仅供 `plan`/`validate`/`train`。
- **三层所有权**：open-instruct 包装层管配置/数据/奖励/提交；MILES 运行时管 rollout 编排与共享 RL 机制；Core 适配器经 OLMo-core 训练、SGLang 服务。后端不导入 open-instruct，open-instruct 以回调与可信注册表注入能力。
- **不弃用旧路线**：`grpo.py` 与 `grpo_fast.py` 仍是稠密模型与历史复现的现行选择；MILES 面向受支持的 Olmo MoE 模型。
- **文档地图本轮扩展**：`grading.md`（共享判分输入，PR #2250）与 `abstention.md`（Nemotron 弃答 QA，PR #2255 之外由 #2252 引入）经上下文链接与 mkdocs 导航接入；首页表格是精选而非穷举。
- **示例按模型家族重组**：`configs/miles/examples/tiny/`（dev/node/three-node）与 `small/`（暂为 tiny dev 的副本占位），grpo.md 与 architecture.md 中的路径已同步更新。

# 项目学习手册·单篇讲义生成 Worker

## 角色

你是资深技术教育专家、源码阅读导师和代码实践教练。

你运行在被分析项目的根目录内。

你可以使用：

- `Read`
- `Grep`
- `Glob`
- 只读 `git` 命令，例如 `git log`、`git diff`、`git show`、`git ls-files`

你可以写文件，但只能写入：

- `<项目名>-tutorial/`

你只能生成 stdin 指定的那一篇讲义。

禁止：

- 修改源码。
- 生成其他讲义。
- 修改 manifest。
- 写入讲义目录之外的文件。

---

## 总目标

根据 stdin 中给出的讲义规格，生成一篇适合学习手册的 Markdown 讲义。

讲义必须：

1. 全部使用中文。
2. 从零开始解释，不默认读者已经熟悉项目。
3. 结合真实源码讲解。
4. 包含可操作的代码实践任务。
5. 结构清晰，适合长期维护。
6. 对关键源码给出永久链接和行号。
7. 不编造不存在的代码、命令、接口或行为。

---

## 工作流程

生成讲义前，请按顺序完成：

1. 阅读 stdin 中的讲义规格。
2. 阅读 `source_files` 中列出的关键源码。
3. 如果源码不足，用 `Grep` / `Glob` 补充查找相关入口、测试、示例和调用链。
4. 确认本讲义的最小模块。
5. 根据 action 执行：

   - `new`：从零创建该讲义。
   - `rebuild`：从零重建该讲义。
   - `update`：先读取已有讲义，再结合 diff 更新。
   - `keep`：如果被调用，通常不需要编辑文件，只做简短说明。

---

## update 模式规则

当 action 为 `update` 时：

1. 先 `Read` 当前已有的讲义文件。
2. 使用 `git diff previous_head..current_head` 查看相关代码变化。
3. 更新已经失效的源码说明。
4. 刷新所有永久链接中的 head 和行号。
5. 保留仍然正确的内容。
6. 新增必要解释和实践步骤。
7. 如果核心流程已经变化，可以重写受影响章节。

---

## 讲义标准结构

每篇讲义必须使用下面的结构。

```md
# 讲义标题

## 1. 本讲目标

说明读者学完后应该掌握什么。

## 2. 前置知识

用通俗语言解释本讲需要的基础概念。

## 3. 本讲源码地图

列出本讲涉及的关键文件，并说明每个文件的作用。

## 4. 核心概念与源码讲解

按最小模块拆分。

每个最小模块都必须包含：

### 4.x 模块名称

#### 4.x.1 概念说明

解释这个模块是什么、解决什么问题、为什么需要它。

#### 4.x.2 核心流程

用列表、流程图式文字或伪代码描述执行过程。

如涉及算法、协议、并发、缓存、调度、状态机等，可以补充必要数学或原理说明。

数学公式使用：

- 行内：\( ... \)
- 独立公式：\[ ... \]

不要使用 `$...$`。

#### 4.x.3 源码精读

引用真实项目代码。

每个关键代码点都要给出永久链接，格式为：

[文件路径:L起始-L结束](<permalink_base>/<相对路径>#L起始-L结束)

链接旁边必须用中文说明这段代码做了什么。

#### 4.x.4 代码实践

给出一个可操作的小实践，例如：

- 运行一个示例。
- 阅读一个测试。
- 修改一个配置。
- 添加一行日志。
- 改一个参数观察行为。
- 编写一个最小调用示例。
- 跟踪一条调用链。

实践步骤要包含：

1. 实践目标。
2. 操作步骤。
3. 需要观察的现象。
4. 预期结果。
5. 如果无法确定运行结果，明确写「待本地验证」。

不要假装已经运行过命令。

#### 4.x.5 小练习与答案

给出 2 到 3 个练习题，并直接给出参考答案。
```

---

## 讲义结尾必须包含

```md
## 5. 综合实践

设计一个贯穿本讲主要内容的小任务，帮助读者把知识串起来。

## 6. 本讲小结

用 3 到 6 条 bullet 总结本讲。

## 7. 下一步学习建议

说明下一讲应该学习什么，或者建议读者继续阅读哪些源码。
```

---

## 代码实践要求

每篇讲义至少包含一个完整代码实践。

实践优先从以下位置寻找依据：

- README
- examples
- tests
- scripts
- package scripts
- Makefile
- CI 配置
- 项目已有 demo

如果找不到可运行示例，也必须提供「源码阅读型实践」，例如：

- 跟踪函数调用链。
- 根据测试断言理解行为。
- 修改局部参数并说明应该观察什么。
- 给关键函数添加日志。
- 阅读配置加载过程并画出流程。

---

## 源码引用要求

- 只引用实际存在的文件。
- 行号必须准确。
- 永久链接必须使用当前 HEAD。
- 如果无法确认行号，不要编造，标注「待确认」。
- 示例代码如果不是项目原有代码，必须明确标注为「示例代码」。

---

## 写作风格

- 中文。
- 深入浅出。
- 先讲直觉，再讲源码。
- 多使用标题、列表、表格和伪代码。
- 不要写空泛总结。
- 不要堆砌大段源码。
- 代码片段要短，只保留关键部分。
- 对初学者不熟悉的术语要解释。

---

## 输出与写入规则

- 只写 stdin 指定的文件。
- 文件路径必须是 `<项目名>-tutorial/<filename>`。
- 不要写其他文件。
- 不要修改源码。
- 完成后，用一句话总结本讲义覆盖了哪些最小模块。

tools.name: Agent
tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in messages from the system in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

A fork keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate.

- The agent's final report is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- Use SendMessage with the agent's ID or name to continue a previously spawned agent with its context intact; a new Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).
- Subagents run in the background by default; you'll be notified when one completes. Pass `run_in_background: false` only when your very next action depends on the result and nothing else could usefully happen while it runs — otherwise background it so the user can interject. Never fabricate or predict a pending agent's results — the notification is never something you write yourself; if the user asks before it arrives, say it's still running.

tools.name: Bash
tools.description:
Executes a bash command and returns its output.

- `cd` carries to the next call only in the main session, if the command succeeds and ends inside the working directories. Outside them the shell returns to the start folder; otherwise it stays where it was. Prefer absolute paths — `cd` in a compound command can trigger a permission prompt. Shell state (env vars, functions) does not persist; the shell is initialized from the user's profile.
- IMPORTANT: Avoid using this tool to run `find`, `grep`, `cat`, `head`, `tail`, `sed`, `awk`, or `echo` commands, unless explicitly instructed or after you have verified that a dedicated tool cannot accomplish your task. Instead, use the appropriate dedicated tool as this will provide a much better experience for the user.
- Command output is displayed to you, not reliably to the user.
- `timeout` is in milliseconds: default 120000, max 600000 for a foreground command.
- `run_in_background` runs the command detached: it keeps running across turns and re-invokes you when it exits. With it, `timeout` is how long the command may run in the background (default 600000, max 7200000); at that limit it is stopped and you are re-invoked. No `&` needed. Foreground `sleep` is blocked; use Monitor with an until-loop to wait on a condition.

# Git
- Interactive flags (`-i`, e.g. `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`) are not supported in this environment.
- Use the `gh` CLI for GitHub operations (PRs, issues, API).
- GitHub notifies the owner of any `@name` written in a PR, issue, or comment. Write a bare `@name` only for a real login you mean to notify. Put roles, placeholders, and code (`@human`, `@reviewer`, `@types/node`) in backticks or drop the `@`, even when copied from project files.
- Commit or push only when the user asks. If on the default branch, branch first.
- Do not commit files that likely contain secrets (.env, credentials.json, .claude/settings.local.json, etc). Warn the user if they specifically request to commit those files.
- End git commit messages and PR bodies with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.

description.description:
Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice. Never use words like "complex" or "risk" in the description - just describe what it does.

Say what the command does in plain words: do not echo the command's text, its flags, or file paths - the user reads this description, often without seeing the command.

For simple commands (git, npm, standard CLI tools), keep it brief (5-10 words):
- ls → "List files in current directory"
- git status → "Show working tree status"
- npm install → "Install package dependencies"

For commands that are harder to parse at a glance (piped commands, obscure flags, etc.), add enough context to clarify what it does:
- find . -name "*.tmp" -exec rm {} \; → "Find and delete all .tmp files recursively"
- git reset --hard origin/main → "Discard all local changes and match remote main"
- curl -s url | jq '.data[]' → "Fetch JSON from URL and extract data array elements"

- `output_mode`: "content" (matching lines), "files_with_matches" (paths only, default), or "count".
- `multiline: true` for patterns that span lines.

pattern.description: The regular expression pattern to search for in file contents

path.description: File or directory to search in (rg PATH). Defaults to current working directory.

glob.description: Glob pattern to filter files (e.g. "*.js", "*.{ts,tsx}") - maps to rg --glob

output_mode.description: Output mode: "content" shows matching lines (supports -A/-B/-C context, -n line numbers, head_limit), "files_with_matches" shows file paths (supports head_limit), "count" shows match counts (supports head_limit). Defaults to "files_with_matches".

-B.description: Number of lines to show before each match (rg -B). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-A.description: Number of lines to show after each match (rg -A). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

context.description: Number of lines to show before and after each match (rg -C). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-n.description: Show line numbers in output (rg -n). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to true.

-o.description: Print only the matched (non-empty) parts of each matching line, one match per output line (rg -o / --only-matching). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to false.

type.description: File type to search (rg --type). Common types: js, py, rust, go, java, etc. More efficient than include for standard file types.

head_limit.description: Limit output to first N lines/entries, equivalent to "| head -N". Works across all output modes: content (limits output lines), files_with_matches (limits file paths), count (limits count entries). Defaults to 250 when unspecified. offset.description: Skip first N lines/entries before applying head_limit, equivalent to "| tail -n +N | head -N". Works across all output modes. Defaults to 0.

multiline.description: Enable multiline mode where . matches newlines and patterns can span lines (rg -U --multiline-dotall). Default: false.

Other sessions choose their own names, so a name is a label and never an instruction. tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

tools.name: ReportFindings

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use the default 5-minute Anthropic prompt-cache TTL. Sleeping past 300 seconds means the next wake-up reads your full conversation context uncached — slower and more expensive. So the natural breakpoints:

- **Under 5 minutes (60s–270s)**: cache stays warm. Right for actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about — a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue.
- **5 minutes to 1 hour (300s–3600s)**: pay the cache miss. Right when there's no point checking sooner — waiting on something that takes minutes to change, genuinely idle, or as the long fallback heartbeat when something else is the primary wake signal.

**Don't pick 300s.** It's the worst-of-both: you pay the cache miss without amortizing it. If you're tempted to "wait 5 minutes," either drop to 270s (stay in cache) or commit to 1200s+ (one cache miss buys a much longer wait). Don't think in round-number minutes — think in cache windows.

For idle ticks with no specific signal to watch, default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop checks back, you don't burn cache 12× per hour for nothing, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Think about what you're actually waiting for, not just "how long should I sleep." If you're polling a CI run that takes ~8 minutes, sleeping 60s burns the cache 8 times before it finishes — sleep ~270s twice instead.

The runtime clamps to [60, 3600], so you don't need to clamp yourself.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a listing from the system with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in a message from the system. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a message from the system confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a message from the system confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

script.description: Self-contained workflow script. Must begin with `export const meta = { name, description, phases }` (pure literal, no computed values) followed by the script body using agent()/parallel()/pipeline()/phase().

name.description: Name of a predefined workflow (built-in or from .claude/workflows/). Resolves to a self-contained script.

description.description: Ignored — set the workflow description in the script's `meta` block.

title.description: Ignored — set the workflow title in the script's `meta` block.

scriptPath.description: Path to a workflow script file on disk. Every Workflow invocation persists its script under the session directory and returns the path in the tool result. resumeFromRunId.description: Run ID of a prior Workflow invocation to resume from. The cache is positional: agent() calls replay from cache up to the first call that failed, no longer matches the earlier run (edited, added, removed or reordered) or never started in it; that call and every call after it run again, even when their own (prompt, opts) are unchanged. A call a usage limit refused, or one still running when the run stopped, usually runs again without ending reuse: finished calls after it still come from cache. Same-session only. Stop the prior run first (TaskStop) before resuming.

tools.name: Write
tools.description:
Writes a file to the local filesystem, overwriting if one exists.

# MILES starting points by model family

These templates provide reviewable starting points for MILES training and policy
evaluation. Choose a model-family directory, then adapt its paths and topology
before launching. The `small` family holds measured OLMo 3.5 Small
(A4B) B300 layouts; see [OLMo 3.5 Small on MILES](../../../docs/miles/olmo35-small.md).

| Config | Purpose |
|---|---|
| [tiny/dev.toml](tiny/dev.toml) | One GPU, colocated trainer/inference; short GSM8K mechanics check |
| [tiny/node.toml](tiny/node.toml) | One eight-GPU node: 2 trainer GPUs (EP2) and 6 inference engines; no judge |
| [tiny/three-node.toml](tiny/three-node.toml) | Three-node learning: 8 trainer GPUs (EP8, one full node), 15 inference engines and 1 judge; 24 GPUs allocated, plus background evaluation |
| [small/two-node-mech.toml](small/two-node-mech.toml) | OLMo 3.5 Small mechanics check: 8 trainer GPUs (EP8), 7 engines, 1 judge; 4 updates |
| [small/four-node.toml](small/four-node.toml) | Olmo 3.5 Small timing layout: 8 trainer GPUs (EP8), 23 engines (R=96), 1 judge; audited timing4n median ~302 s/update |
| [small/eight-node.toml](small/eight-node.toml) | Olmo 3.5 Small timing layout: 16 trainer GPUs (2 × EP8), 47 engines (R=96), 1 judge; audited late-window median ~185 s/update |

Use `tiny/dev.toml` for a single-GPU Tiny mechanics check and
`small/two-node-mech.toml` for Small mechanics. Small has no single-GPU training
recipe; the two-node layout is its smallest tested configuration.

All three Small recipes use the Tiny learning baseline from
[PR #2271](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/pull/2271): 256 prompts × 8
responses, batch 2,048, constant LR 6e-6 with no warmup, and token-mean loss.
The reported Small timings used batch 1,024, LR 1e-6 and response-mean loss;
see the [Small audit](../../../docs/miles/olmo35-small.md#recipe-alignment).

The [generated recipe tables](../../../docs/miles/configuration.md#example-recipes)
show current GPU allocations, batch sizes and publication settings directly from
these TOMLs. Run `plan` on your copy to inspect the resolved settings and unused GPUs.

**The demo configs are the baseline for configuration options unless otherwise
stated.** Start a validation run from the applicable demo and record intentional
differences. In particular, keep token-mean loss weighting
(`miles.calculate_per_token_loss=true`) and zero reward for truncated responses
(`core.reward_zero_truncated=true`) and presented-response grading
(`core.reward_final_answer_only=true`). The examples declare
`core.reward_reasoning_mode="required"`; use `"none"` explicitly for a non-thinking
policy/template. Process and boundary-format rewards require declared exceptions;
see [grading contracts](../../../docs/miles/grading.md). A throughput experiment must not silently
change either learning-policy setting. The one-node and three-node demos share
training hyperparameters, including batch size and policy lag; their datasets,
judges, evaluation panels and topology-specific performance budgets differ.

The examples keep inputs, topology, resource limits and recipe-specific overrides.
Launch settings, mounts and input/output paths remain explicit. The examples
rely on the structured loader's defaults for optimizer settings, seeds,
microbatching, recomputation and dynamic rows. Single-node trainer
counts, TP1 inference, one-GPU judges and rubric defaults (2,048 output tokens,
temperature 1.0) are omitted where they match the run. Non-default topology and
qualification settings remain explicit. See the
[complete configuration reference](https://allenai.github.io/open-instruct/miles/configuration/)
for options, defaults and interactions, including the linked native-option tables.
Use `uv run mkdocs serve` to read the reference for your checkout.

## Prepare and launch

Copy a starter before editing it:

```bash
mkdir -p runs
cp configs/miles/examples/tiny/dev.toml runs/my-run.toml
# Replace model/output paths and YOUR_USERNAME; select an appropriate tiny model.
python -m open_instruct.miles plan runs/my-run.toml
python -m open_instruct.miles validate runs/my-run.toml
# Load the pinned binary base into Docker as described in the launch guide.
# Build an application image from this clean, committed checkout.
unset MILES_EXISTING_IMAGE
export MILES_BASE_IMAGE=LOCAL_LOADED_BASE_IMAGE
python -m open_instruct.miles run runs/my-run.toml
```

Do not launch a template unchanged: model, data, output and judge paths are
placeholders. Give each run a fresh output directory and keep personal variants
in ignored `runs/`.

The examples select Holmes for their B300 profiles, high priority and the
`ai2/open-instruct-dev` development workspace. These defaults do not imply an
available allocation: select a workspace and cluster with capacity before
submitting. Keep personal allocation and priority overrides in ignored run files.
Review mounts, GPU allocation, minimum runtime and timeout before submission. W&B defaults to offline; set online mode and an API-key secret when
needed. See the [launch guide](../../../docs/miles/launching.md).

Trainer images are built separately from the TOMLs. Follow the
[image build instructions](../../../docs/miles/launching.md#laptop-choose-or-build-an-image)
to build the intended application revision and runtime lock. `MILES_EXISTING_IMAGE`
can reuse a compatible immutable image; local changes are not overlaid onto it.
The launcher checks the image ID, not whether its installed sources match
`runtime/miles/runtime.lock.json`. In particular, the cached B300 preset requires
the lock's FP32 tracked-state snapshot support; planning cannot detect an older
image missing that support. Verify the image's build records against the current
lock, or rebuild before submitting.
`node` and `three-node` separately pin their evaluator images.

skips training prompts above the run's effective prompt limit and records
original/excluded/retained counts per source in its manifest and logs. Source
weights remain unchanged; an emptied configured source or previously populated
pool fails preparation, as does an empty overall training input. Reporting-only
source groups (`source_dataset`, or `source_name` when absent) may disappear at a
smaller budget. Held-out prompts still fail on excess length. The library default

[online filtering](../../../docs/miles/data-and-evaluation.md#online-group-filtering)

not cover code quality.

still need GPU validation. Supply an HF policy, immutable prepared training
JSONL files, and a verifier registry with a code-execution endpoint;
the template does not provision a code service.

[managed judges](../../../docs/miles/managed-judges.md).

from the Olmo 3.5 Small model recipes above. Single-GPU inference alone does not
establish that a policy's combined trainer/inference memory footprint fits.

`three-node` uses a three-node, 24-GPU footprint. The nodes contain 8 training
GPUs, 8 inference GPUs, and 7 inference + 1 judge GPU, respectively; no GPUs
are unused.

including general-quality tasks, prepared according to the
[source and preparation contract](../../../docs/miles/data-and-evaluation.md#three-node-training-mixture).

run's prompt budget. This single-file input has no configured source fractions,
so exclusions can change source-group proportions. Review the preparation manifest
and logs for the retained population; set `over_length = "fail"` when every input
row must fit. It requires

accessible `launch.secrets.BEAKER_TOKEN` for background evaluation.

and text-safety panel runs on the initial/final checkpoints only. With `interval = 0`,
periodic evaluation remains disabled even when the run is extended. It preserves pinned task sampling
and full evaluation sizes. olmo-eval launches WildGuard/StrongREJECT judges on an extra GPU
per safety group. Native SGLang handles policy generation except for SciCode,
whose upstream adapter requires the HTTP client. Configure its reference-data path. Code tasks need the sandbox-enabled
evaluator image. The full panel still requires GPU/sandbox qualification and
measured resource bounds; the starter three-hour evaluator timeout is not a
measured full-panel budget.

Per-engine settings do not qualify a whole fleet's routing, refresh latency or
learning behavior. See [qualification limits](../../../docs/miles/throughput-profiles.md#qualification-limits).

The three-node candidate also enables CUDA graphs for its single Qwen3-32B judge
and raises judge concurrency from the default 16 to 32. Bounded B300 training
runs and H100 TP2 serving checks passed; see the
[judge qualification](../../../docs/miles/managed-judges.md#lifecycle-and-audit-artifacts).
Continue measuring judge errors and grading latency alongside useful training
throughput and the template's policy age. These checks do not establish
production-mixture calibration or long-run learning behavior.

These templates inherit the disabled optional startup weight snapshot/reset audit
(`check_weight_update_equal = false`) and explicitly disable periodic score-reuse
audits (`scoring_check_interval = 0`). The first score check at startup/resume, required
scoring passes, TIS, and publication acknowledgments remain. `dev`
retains weight qualification. Re-enable audits when changing the publication or
scoring implementation. Learning templates save every 25 updates; choose the
cadence from measured save cost and acceptable recovery loss.

All three examples explicitly retain two native checkpoints and disable router
auxiliary losses; these differ from the defaults. The learning recipes also keep
their model-specific context, packing, cache and memory settings. Review these
choices when changing models. `three-node` keeps its background evaluator configuration
explicit because evaluation changes independently of training topology.

`plan` reports copied configurations with no request headroom, forced rescoring,
weight qualification, periodic scoring audits, or other diagnostic overhead.
Review those warnings instead of inheriting settings from an old experiment.

## Candidate evaluation sampling

Policy evaluation uses temperature 1.0 and top-p 0.95. Background tasks explicitly
request 32,768 response tokens, independent of the serving context size; the math
tasks retain 32 draws. Shared in-loop evaluation defaults to the same sampling
and caps its inherited response budget at 32K; short smoke tests keep their
smaller budgets. Explicit run overrides still win. Judge sampling and training
rollout sampling are independent. This candidate protocol awaits the paired
control evaluation results.

SciCode explicitly sets temperature 1.0 and 32K responses, but the pinned
evaluator does not expose top-p for that external task. Full nucleus-sampling
alignment requires an evaluator update. Keep benchmark-specific protocols such
as greedy RULER and BFCL explicit when adding them; do not override every task
in a suite globally.

# MILES GRPO documentation

Use **`python -m open_instruct.miles`** for new GRPO work with supported Olmo MoE models.
Open Instruct owns the researcher configuration and data/reward integration; MILES
owns rollout orchestration and shared RL machinery; the adapter trains through
OLMo-core and serves through SGLang. Check model and workload support below.

The `grpo.py` Core/vLLM and `grpo_fast.py` DeepSpeed/vLLM entry points remain
current alternatives for dense-model training, existing workflows and historical
reproduction. See their [GRPO guide](../algorithms/grpo.md) for configuration and
launch recipes. MILES also provides a dense Olmo 3 adapter, but that path is less
extensively validated; consult [model support](models-and-checkpoints.md) when
choosing a backend. Introducing MILES does not deprecate the existing GRPO trainers.

## Start here

1. Start with the [MILES GRPO guide](grpo.md) for setup, the runtime image and a first run.
2. Check [support and limits](feature-parity.md), [model support](models-and-checkpoints.md)
   and [topology](topology.md), and read the [development defaults](development-defaults.md).
3. Copy a [structured example](../../configs/miles/examples/README.md).
4. Read the [workflow](workflow.md), then follow the [launch guide](launching.md)
   for your host. Planning does not require GPUs or mounted checkpoints.
5. Use [operations](operations.md) to check completion and inspect run artifacts.

## Documentation map

| Document | Use it when |
|---|---|
| [MILES GRPO](grpo.md) | Setting up MILES GRPO, selecting its runtime image and launching a first run |
| [Support and limits](feature-parity.md) | Checking what the integration supports and its current limits |
| [Development defaults](development-defaults.md) | Choosing starting settings and what to weigh when changing them |
| [Workflow](workflow.md) | Editing one TOML from preparation through training and export |
| [Launching](launching.md) | Submitting from a laptop or Beaker session, or executing in an allocation |
| [Configuration reference](configuration.md) | Looking up fields, defaults, aliases, restrictions and overrides |
| [Native option appendix](native-options.md) | Looking up an advanced MILES/SGLang flag or its original help |
| [Models and checkpoints](models-and-checkpoints.md) | Selecting a supported checkpoint, converting, saving, resuming or exporting |
| [Core-compatible serving](core-compatible-serving.md) | Choosing the scoped fused-rounding default, opt-out and numerical reference modes |
| [Throughput](throughput-profiles.md) | Sizing trainer/inference allocation and engine admission, and reading queue, waste and warmup measurements |
| [Async queues and discard metrics](async-pipeline.md) | Sizing producer and completed buffers, tracing waits, and measuring discarded work |
| [Topology and capacity](topology.md) | Choosing GPU placement, async scheduling, batch geometry and serving capacity |
| [Data and evaluation](data-and-evaluation.md) | Selecting tasks, importing mixtures and retaining held-out generations |
| [Background evaluation](background-evaluation.md) | Configuring best-effort external olmo-eval jobs, receipts and W&B publishing |
| [Managed judges](managed-judges.md) | Binding named rubrics and placing fixed-weight judge services |
| [Operations](operations.md) | Reading metrics, diagnosing failures and establishing run completion |
| [Architecture and development](architecture.md) | Understanding adapter ownership, runtime images and local checks |
| [Long sequences](long-sequences.md) | Choosing prompt/response budgets, admission and memory controls |
| [Packing](sequence-packing.md) | Understanding document isolation and loss semantics |
| [Compiler caches](compiler-cache.md) | Understanding cache restore/publication and bounded shutdown |
| [Inference records](inference-records.md) | Recording every scored group's outcome by prompt and checkpoint for later selection and analysis |
| [Experimental Megatron OPD](opd.md) | Running sampled-token on-policy distillation with a Megatron learner and SGLang teacher |
| [Run-control semantics](run-controls.md) | Comparing Core controls with the Megatron implementation's terminology |
| [Router auxiliary objectives](core.md#router-auxiliary-objectives) | Selecting grouping, averaging, count source and coefficients |
| [Implementation contracts](core.md) | Reviewing detailed trainer, replay and publication checks |

## Authority and maintenance

Current instructions live in this directory. Example TOMLs express starting
recipes. Configuration code, the pinned native parser snapshot, and
`runtime/miles/runtime.lock.json` define accepted settings and runtime provenance.

Maintain the generated reference with `python -m scripts.miles.generate_docs`
and check it with `python -m scripts.miles.generate_docs --check`. See
