1	# MILES starting points by model family
2	
3	These templates provide reviewable starting points for MILES training and policy
4	evaluation. Choose a model-family directory, then adapt its paths and topology
5	before launching. The `small` family holds measured OLMo 3.5 Small
6	(A4B) B300 layouts; see [OLMo 3.5 Small on MILES](../../../docs/miles/olmo35-small.md).
7	
8	| Config | Purpose |
9	|---|---|
10	| [tiny/dev.toml](tiny/dev.toml) | One GPU, colocated trainer/inference; short GSM8K mechanics check |
11	| [tiny/node.toml](tiny/node.toml) | One eight-GPU node: 2 trainer GPUs (EP2) and 6 inference engines; no judge |
12	| [tiny/three-node.toml](tiny/three-node.toml) | Three-node learning: 8 trainer GPUs (EP8, one full node), 15 inference engines and 1 judge; 24 GPUs allocated, plus background evaluation |
13	| [small/two-node-mech.toml](small/two-node-mech.toml) | OLMo 3.5 Small mechanics check: 8 trainer GPUs (EP8), 7 engines, 1 judge; 4 updates |
14	| [small/four-node.toml](small/four-node.toml) | Olmo 3.5 Small timing layout: 8 trainer GPUs (EP8), 23 engines (R=96), 1 judge; audited timing4n median ~302 s/update |
15	| [small/eight-node.toml](small/eight-node.toml) | Olmo 3.5 Small timing layout: 16 trainer GPUs (2 × EP8), 47 engines (R=96), 1 judge; audited late-window median ~185 s/update |
16	
17	Use `tiny/dev.toml` for a single-GPU Tiny mechanics check and
18	`small/two-node-mech.toml` for Small mechanics. Small has no single-GPU training
19	recipe; the two-node layout is its smallest tested configuration.
20	
21	All three Small recipes use the Tiny learning baseline from
22	[PR #2271](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/pull/2271): 256 prompts × 8
23	responses, batch 2,048, constant LR 6e-6 with no warmup, and token-mean loss.
24	The reported Small timings used batch 1,024, LR 1e-6 and response-mean loss;
25	see the [Small audit](../../../docs/miles/olmo35-small.md#recipe-alignment).
26	
27	The [generated recipe tables](../../../docs/miles/configuration.md#example-recipes)
28	show current GPU allocations, batch sizes and publication settings directly from
29	these TOMLs. Run `plan` on your copy to inspect the resolved settings and unused GPUs.
30	
31	**The demo configs are the baseline for configuration options unless otherwise
32	stated.** Start a validation run from the applicable demo and record intentional
33	differences. In particular, keep token-mean loss weighting
34	(`miles.calculate_per_token_loss=true`) and zero reward for truncated responses
35	(`core.reward_zero_truncated=true`) and presented-response grading
36	(`core.reward_final_answer_only=true`). The examples declare
37	`core.reward_reasoning_mode="required"`; use `"none"` explicitly for a non-thinking
38	policy/template. Process and boundary-format rewards require declared exceptions;
39	see [grading contracts](../../../docs/miles/grading.md). A throughput experiment must not silently
40	change either learning-policy setting. The one-node and three-node demos share
41	training hyperparameters, including batch size and policy lag; their datasets,
42	judges, evaluation panels and topology-specific performance budgets differ.
43	
44	The examples keep inputs, topology, resource limits and recipe-specific overrides.
45	Launch settings, mounts and input/output paths remain explicit. The examples
46	rely on the structured loader's defaults for optimizer settings, seeds,
47	microbatching, recomputation and dynamic rows. Single-node trainer
48	counts, TP1 inference, one-GPU judges and rubric defaults (2,048 output tokens,
49	temperature 1.0) are omitted where they match the run. Non-default topology and
50	qualification settings remain explicit. See the
51	[complete configuration reference](https://allenai.github.io/open-instruct/miles/configuration/)
52	for options, defaults and interactions, including the linked native-option tables.
53	Use `uv run mkdocs serve` to read the reference for your checkout.
54	
55	## Prepare and launch
56	
57	Copy a starter before editing it:
58	
59	```bash
60	mkdir -p runs
61	cp configs/miles/examples/tiny/dev.toml runs/my-run.toml
62	# Replace model/output paths and YOUR_USERNAME; select an appropriate tiny model.
63	python -m open_instruct.miles plan runs/my-run.toml
64	python -m open_instruct.miles validate runs/my-run.toml
65	# Load the pinned binary base into Docker as described in the launch guide.
66	# Build an application image from this clean, committed checkout.
67	unset MILES_EXISTING_IMAGE
68	export MILES_BASE_IMAGE=LOCAL_LOADED_BASE_IMAGE
69	python -m open_instruct.miles run runs/my-run.toml
70	```
71	
72	Do not launch a template unchanged: model, data, output and judge paths are
73	placeholders. Give each run a fresh output directory and keep personal variants
74	in ignored `runs/`.
75	
76	The examples select Holmes for their B300 profiles, high priority and the
77	`ai2/open-instruct-dev` development workspace. These defaults do not imply an
78	available allocation: select a workspace and cluster with capacity before
79	submitting. Keep personal allocation and priority overrides in ignored run files.
80	Review mounts, GPU allocation, minimum runtime and timeout before submission. W&B defaults to offline; set online mode and an API-key secret when
81	needed. See the [launch guide](../../../docs/miles/launching.md).
82	
83	Trainer images are built separately from the TOMLs. Follow the
84	[image build instructions](../../../docs/miles/launching.md#laptop-choose-or-build-an-image)
85	to build the intended application revision and runtime lock. `MILES_EXISTING_IMAGE`
86	can reuse a compatible immutable image; local changes are not overlaid onto it.
87	The launcher checks the image ID, not whether its installed sources match
88	`runtime/miles/runtime.lock.json`. In particular, the cached B300 preset requires
89	the lock's FP32 tracked-state snapshot support; planning cannot detect an older
90	image missing that support. Verify the image's build records against the current
91	lock, or rebuild before submitting.
92	`node` and `three-node` separately pin their evaluator images.
93	
94	## Inputs and expected outputs
95	
96	All three examples explicitly set `data.over_length = "exclude"`, so preparation
97	skips training prompts above the run's effective prompt limit and records
98	original/excluded/retained counts per source in its manifest and logs. Source
99	weights remain unchanged; an emptied configured source or previously populated
100	pool fails preparation, as does an empty overall training input. Reporting-only
101	source groups (`source_dataset`, or `source_name` when absent) may disappear at a
102	smaller budget. Held-out prompts still fail on excess length. The library default
103	remains `"fail"`; remove this example override or set it to `"fail"` to reject
104	over-limit training prompts too.
105	
106	`dev` retains its compatible tiny-checkpoint placeholder and short GSM8K workload.
107	It exercises preparation,
108	generation, training, shared-engine evaluation, native checkpoint saving and final
109	HF export. It is a mechanics check, not an accuracy baseline. A completed run does
110	not test interrupted-run recovery. Filtering is disabled in this example
111	because a tiny model may produce only constant rewards; see
112	[online filtering](../../../docs/miles/data-and-evaluation.md#online-group-filtering)
113	before changing this for a learning run.
114	
115	`node` adapts the previous two-node `medium` learning recipe to one B300 node,
116	using two EP2 trainer ranks and six TP1 inference engines, with no judge.
117	Its prepared workload contains math, instruction-following and code tasks only;
118	exclude general-quality and other judge-dependent verifiers from training files. The paths use a separate `math-ifeval-code` preparation.
119	Its background GSM8K, GSM8K-Platinum and IFBench panel runs initially, every
120	50 optimizer updates, and finally, using a separate one-GPU allocation. Set
121	`launch.secrets.BEAKER_TOKEN` to enable submission. These starter benchmarks do
122	not cover code quality.
123	This topology passes CPU planning checks; sustained throughput and memory fit
124	still need GPU validation. Supply an HF policy, immutable prepared training
125	JSONL files, and a verifier registry with a code-execution endpoint;
126	the template does not provision a code service.
127	See [datasets and verifiers](../../../docs/miles/data-and-evaluation.md) and
128	[managed judges](../../../docs/miles/managed-judges.md).
129	
130	The former topology tier named `small` is retired. For Tiny, use `tiny/dev.toml`
131	for mechanics and `tiny/node.toml` for disaggregated learning. These are distinct
132	from the Olmo 3.5 Small model recipes above. Single-GPU inference alone does not
133	establish that a policy's combined trainer/inference memory footprint fits.
134	
135	`three-node` uses a three-node, 24-GPU footprint. The nodes contain 8 training
136	GPUs, 8 inference GPUs, and 7 inference + 1 judge GPU, respectively; no GPUs
137	are unused.
138	Its starting input is the full published `allenai/Dolci-Think-RL-7B` mixture,
139	including general-quality tasks, prepared according to the
140	[source and preparation contract](../../../docs/miles/data-and-evaluation.md#three-node-training-mixture).
141	The example's explicit `over_length = "exclude"` keeps the subset that fits the
142	run's prompt budget. This single-file input has no configured source fractions,
143	so exclusions can change source-group proportions. Review the preparation manifest
144	and logs for the retained population; set `over_length = "fail"` when every input
145	row must fit. It requires
146	a prepared Qwen3-32B judge with named verifier bindings. It also requires an
147	accessible `launch.secrets.BEAKER_TOKEN` for background evaluation.
148	Evaluator jobs allocate GPUs beyond the training plan;
149	overlapping jobs can increase that total. Its 25-entry post-training development
150	and text-safety panel runs on the initial/final checkpoints only. With `interval = 0`,
151	periodic evaluation remains disabled even when the run is extended. It preserves pinned task sampling
152	and full evaluation sizes. olmo-eval launches WildGuard/StrongREJECT judges on an extra GPU
153	per safety group. Native SGLang handles policy generation except for SciCode,
154	whose upstream adapter requires the HTTP client. Configure its reference-data path. Code tasks need the sandbox-enabled
155	evaluator image. The full panel still requires GPU/sandbox qualification and
156	measured resource bounds; the starter three-hour evaluator timeout is not a
157	measured full-panel budget.
158	With offline W&B, sync training and manually publish the retained evaluation results.
159	Snapshot cleanup is manual after all referencing jobs stop. See
160	[background evaluation](../../../docs/miles/background-evaluation.md) for the
161	protocol, outputs and limits.
162	
163	For either learning template, check model memory and service capacity before
164	scaling. The [throughput guide](../../../docs/miles/throughput-profiles.md) explains
165	how to size memory budgets and engine admission for a model. Follow the
166	[completion checks](../../../docs/miles/operations.md) to verify training,
167	checkpoint and export outputs.
168	
169	## Capacity and qualification settings
170	
171	The three-node throughput candidate uses 256 prompts × 8 samples per collection
172	and one 2,048-sample optimizer batch at constant LR 6e-6 with policy lag 12. It admits
173	3,840 unfinished samples and keeps up to 1,024 completed prompt groups (8,192 samples), and runs 16 HTTP actors per node
174	with one Ray CPU each. The rollout executor reserves two Ray CPUs and each node
175	advertises 64 logical Ray CPUs through `launch.env.OI_MILES_RAY_CPUS` (default
176	32 when omitted). The node example uses the same worker counts and reservations.
177	Both learning examples set `expandable_segments:True` only on trainer ranks.
178	These reservations permit actor placement; they
179	do not make the Python producer event loop parallel. Distributed HTTP actors
180	parse JSON before producer receipt. The single managed Qwen3-32B judge uses CUDA
181	graphs and a maximum of 32 concurrent calls.
182	
183	These are a bundled candidate, not a measured optimum. Increasing the buffer
184	retains more host memory and older work; keep policy lag bounded and watch stale
185	group discards. The one-node validation has a different layout (2 trainers,
186	5 engines and 1 judge) from the judge-free `node.toml` example. It does not
187	qualify three-node throughput. Keep cold compilation, periodic scoring,
188	evaluation and checkpoint cost separate from steady-state measurements.
189	
190	Background evaluation independently sets `evaluation.provider_kwargs.profile` to
191	`"olmo3.5-12.5b"`. It resolves the optimized settings on the assigned evaluator GPU
192	(including H100 80GB and B300), enables full decode graphs, and sizes native
193	harness batches by engine sequence capacity, counting pass@k expansion. SciCode's
194	HTTP server uses the same profile. See the
195	[evaluation guide](../../../docs/miles/background-evaluation.md) for compatibility,
196	batch-boundary limits and full-panel qualification still required.
197	
198	The learning examples pin `inference.profile = "olmo35-b300-12.5@0.8"` on Holmes.
199	This is the current recommended B300 starting point, based on the experiments
200	below. The suffix is **total@active parameters in billions**: approximately
201	12.5B total and 0.8B active per token for the measured model, including embeddings
202	and the output head. The planner recommends one current preset per GPU. The old
203	B300 v1 preset remains only for reproducing older cached configurations.
204	The preset sets **512 running requests, 512 HTTP permits and decode graphs through
205	batch 512 per engine**, 17,825,792 KV tokens, 3,072 recurrent slots, memory fraction
206	0.7 and prefill chunks of 8,192. It disables cross-request radix caching.
207	Both learning examples set `miles.pause_generation_mode = "in_place"`: active
208	requests keep their attention KV and hybrid recurrent state across weight updates,
209	avoiding re-prefill of their generated prefixes. The original `olmo35-b300-v1`
210	preset still enables radix caching with `extra_buffer` and requires retract mode.
211	Runs started from the old examples must resume with their recorded settings;
212	switching profile or pause/cache mode under the same `output.root` fails the
213	recovery configuration check. Use a new root for the updated recipe.
214	The one-GPU colocated `dev.toml` explicitly keeps retract mode; retained state
215	requires dedicated inference GPUs. See the [retained-state qualification](../../../docs/miles/throughput-profiles.md#retained-state-weight-publication).
216	Cached hybrid serving requires FP32 tracked-state snapshots in the pinned
217	[runtime](../../../runtime/miles/runtime.lock.json); rebuild the image when its
218	pins change. See [model limits](../../../docs/miles/moe-model-support.md#current-limits).
219	
220	To move an example to Jupiter, change both the cluster and profile to
221	`olmo35-h100-12.5@0.8`. This preset also uses admission/HTTP/graph batch 512 and prefill
222	chunks of 8,192, but disables caching and uses 6,684,672 KV tokens, 512 recurrent
223	slots and memory fraction 0.9. Both presets require the studied BF16 Olmo 3.5
224	geometry, dedicated TP1 engines and 34,816 context / 32,768 response caps.
225	The old `olmo35-h100-v1` name remains a compatibility alias for the H100 preset.
226	These settings are starting points, not universal memory-fit or throughput guarantees.
227	
228	Named presets apply whole. Any explicit preset-owned key conflicts, even an equal
229	value; errors show the offending keys, an editable TOML block, and two exits:
230	remove the keys to keep the preset, or select `generic` and manage the settings.
231	Known hardware/topology mismatches fail during planning. Model geometry is checked
232	when actual checkpoint metadata is readable and must pass after preparation before
233	training. Preset settings remain identical before and after preparation.
234	
235	Omitted or `generic` profiles preserve generic defaults and explicit settings.
236	The default recurrent pool is 128 slots. A separately measured **cache-off B300
237	alternative uses 1,024 recurrent slots**; it predates the retained-state learning
238	qualification and is an explicit generic-mode experiment, not the current default.
239	Use the named B300 preset for the qualified learning baseline: its 3,072-slot pool
240	was deliberately kept fixed from the prior profile for those runs. SGLang still
241	allocates all explicitly requested slots with radix off; the inherited
242	`extra_buffer` strategy has no effect while radix is disabled. Reducing the pool
243	could save memory but needs separate retained-state qualification before changing
244	the recommendation. A cached-320 H100 alternative uses 4,456,448 KV tokens and 1,920
245	recurrent slots and likewise requires explicit generic settings. Neither alternative
246	is selected automatically. `dev` retains its explicit small colocated configuration.
247	
248	The planner offers read-only tips when a preset matches or explicit pools resemble
249	a preset for different hardware. Tips appear in a stderr box and
250	`plan.runtime.inference_profile.tips`; routine warnings remain plain lines.
251	A cache-off recommendation for retract mode explicitly notes that it disables
252	prefix reuse; compatibility is not a claim of higher throughput for that mode.
253	There is no `auto` selector. Topology, metrics, producer budget and trainer controls
254	remain separate. To experiment, follow
255	[departing from a preset](../../../docs/miles/throughput-profiles.md#deliberately-departing-from-a-preset).
256	Generic mode does not resize pools, estimate memory fit or retain a hardware pin.
257	
258	The node example explicitly limits unfinished samples to **1,024**, independently
259	of the six engines' 3,072 reserved running slots. Filling every reserved slot is
260	useful only when the trainer can consume the resulting work. Compare trainer wait,
261	useful throughput and stale-work discards before increasing the budget.
262	
263	The unfinished-sample budget, when omitted, is
264	`max(collection samples, 2 × engines × min(HTTP permits, running admission))`,
265	rounded to complete prompt groups. The three-node example explicitly uses
266	**3,840** unfinished samples (256 per engine) as a candidate throughput budget. Removing the
267	explicit limits would give 6,144 for node and 15,360 for three-node. Generic
268	64-admission configurations with omitted budgets give
269	1,024 and 1,920 for those topologies. Explicit
270	`async.async_max_concurrent_samples` wins. Completed siblings can remain outside
271	the unfinished budget, so this is not a limit on all retained responses.
272	
273	Both Tiny learning examples use 256 prompts × 8 responses, batch 2,048,
274	constant LR 6e-6 and lag 12.
275	Node buffers one completed batch; three-node buffers four. The three-node
276	unfinished-sample budget represents 1.875 batches;
277	adding the completed buffer gives 5.875 nominal batches. Sample backfill can retain
278	additional finished siblings, so this arithmetic is not an age guarantee. It is headroom, not
279	a measured optimum or a guarantee of steady throughput. Full-recipe
280	collection and judging can limit throughput even with spare engine capacity.
281	Batch-equivalents do not predict actual policy age or drain duration.
282	Measure trainer wait, useful throughput, oldest-token age and stale-work discards;
283	reduce the producer budget or fleet when production outruns useful consumption.
284	Per-engine settings do not qualify a whole fleet's routing, refresh latency or
285	learning behavior. See [qualification limits](../../../docs/miles/throughput-profiles.md#qualification-limits).
286	
287	The three-node candidate also enables CUDA graphs for its single Qwen3-32B judge
288	and raises judge concurrency from the default 16 to 32. Bounded B300 training
289	runs and H100 TP2 serving checks passed; see the
290	[judge qualification](../../../docs/miles/managed-judges.md#lifecycle-and-audit-artifacts).
291	Continue measuring judge errors and grading latency alongside useful training
292	throughput and the template's policy age. These checks do not establish
293	production-mixture calibration or long-run learning behavior.
294	
295	These templates inherit the disabled optional startup weight snapshot/reset audit
296	(`check_weight_update_equal = false`) and explicitly disable periodic score-reuse
297	audits (`scoring_check_interval = 0`). The first score check at startup/resume, required
298	scoring passes, TIS, and publication acknowledgments remain. `dev`
299	retains weight qualification. Re-enable audits when changing the publication or
300	scoring implementation. Learning templates save every 25 updates; choose the
301	cadence from measured save cost and acceptable recovery loss.
302	
303	All three examples explicitly retain two native checkpoints and disable router
304	auxiliary losses; these differ from the defaults. The learning recipes also keep
305	their model-specific context, packing, cache and memory settings. Review these
306	choices when changing models. `three-node` keeps its background evaluator configuration
307	explicit because evaluation changes independently of training topology.
308	
309	`plan` reports copied configurations with no request headroom, forced rescoring,
310	weight qualification, periodic scoring audits, or other diagnostic overhead.
311	Review those warnings instead of inheriting settings from an old experiment.
312	
313	## Candidate evaluation sampling
314	
315	Policy evaluation uses temperature 1.0 and top-p 0.95. Background tasks explicitly
316	request 32,768 response tokens, independent of the serving context size; the math
317	tasks retain 32 draws. Shared in-loop evaluation defaults to the same sampling
318	and caps its inherited response budget at 32K; short smoke tests keep their
319	smaller budgets. Explicit run overrides still win. Judge sampling and training
320	rollout sampling are independent. This candidate protocol awaits the paired
321	control evaluation results.
322	
323	SciCode explicitly sets temperature 1.0 and 32K responses, but the pinned
324	evaluator does not expose top-p for that external task. Full nucleus-sampling
325	alignment requires an evaluator update. Keep benchmark-specific protocols such
326	as greedy RULER and BFCL explicit when adding them; do not override every task
327	in a suite globally.

81	Learning runs enable `training.filter_zero_std_groups=true`: constant-reward prompt
82	groups are dropped and generation replenishes the accepted training batch. Offline
83	correctness preprocessing can still be applied. The tiny `dev` mechanics
84	example explicitly disables filtering to permit all-zero-reward checks. See
85	[data and evaluation](data-and-evaluation.md#online-group-filtering) for metrics,
86	batch semantics and the opt-out.
87	
88	## Truncated responses
89	
90	The demo configs are the baseline for configuration choices unless a run explicitly
91	states otherwise. The examples use **token-mean loss weighting** and **zero reward for
92	length-truncated responses**. The Core reward default also scores truncations zero,
93	so omitting the field does not silently change the objective. The examples make
94	these choices explicit:
95	
96	```toml
97	[core]
98	reward_zero_truncated = true
99	
100	[miles]
101	calculate_per_token_loss = true
102	```
103	
104	This works with every verifier, managed judges included. It cannot be combined
105	with a `custom_reward_post_process_path` other than the default ungraded-response
106	exclusion described below. Final-answer selection and explicit verifier exceptions
107	are described in [Grading inputs and changes](grading.md).
108	
109	## Ungraded responses
110	
111	A verifier or judge request can fail for reasons unrelated to the response: a
112	code-service outage, a judge transport error, an unparseable verdict. That
113	response has no grade. Scoring it zero would place a correct answer below its
114	siblings' baseline and push the policy away from it; dropping its prompt group
115	would waste every graded sibling. By default (`core.exclude_ungraded = true`) the
116	compiler installs
117	`custom_reward_post_process_path = "open_instruct.miles.rewards.exclusion.exclude_ungraded"`:
118	the ungraded response gets zero advantage and a zeroed loss mask, its group's
119	baseline uses only the graded responses, and the paired group filter ignores it
120	when checking reward variation (groups with fewer than two graded responses are
121	dropped). The failed response keeps `metadata.reward_omission` with the verifier
122	name and error, and W&B reports `rollout/verification/ungraded_samples` and
123	`ungraded_fraction` per collection. With response-averaged loss, excluded responses
124	still count in the batch denominator, so a high failure fraction reduces the
125	policy-gradient signal per step. Groups with no trainable responses are
126	always rejected, even with `filter_zero_std_groups=false`; that setting keeps
127	valid all-zero grades, not empty groups. The collector requests replacement groups.
128	A run where every group is rejected makes no optimizer progress.
129	
130	Set `core.exclude_ungraded = false` to return to omitting the whole prompt group
131	(`rollout/verification/omitted_records`). The compiler also leaves the hook out
132	under `core.expert_balanced_packing`, which supports no reward post-process, and
133	under `miles.partial_rollout`, since the hook supports single-segment rollouts
134	only. Custom multi-segment generators must explicitly opt out as well. A custom
135	`miles.custom_convert_samples_to_train_data_path` bypasses reward postprocessing:
136	it retains group omission, and explicitly combining it with a managed exclusion
137	hook is rejected. Math verifier timeouts and code-service rejections (4xx, or a 500 that
138	persists through its retries) are not ungraded: they keep their zero reward, as
139	documented under [reward-service failure policies](data-and-evaluation.md#reward-service-failure-policies).
140	
141	For an explicitly documented overlong-filtering experiment that excludes truncated
142	responses from training instead, override the baseline with:
143	
144	```toml
145	[core]
146	reward_zero_truncated = false
147	
148	[miles]
149	custom_reward_post_process_path = "open_instruct.miles.rewards.truncation.exclude_truncated"
150	```
151	
152	Truncated responses then get zero advantage and a zeroed loss mask, and each group's
153	baseline uses only its finished, graded responses (this hook also excludes
154	ungraded responses). Raw reward metrics are unchanged. With response-averaged
155	loss, excluded responses still count in the batch denominator. When zero-variance
156	group filtering is enabled, it also considers only finished, graded responses:
157	groups with fewer than two of them or no variation in their rewards are dropped
158	before occupying training batch slots.
159	
160	## Final-answer-only rewards
161	
162	Set `core.reward_final_answer_only=true` to grade only text after the last literal
163	`</think>` by default. A missing closing marker, whitespace-only final answer or
164	reopened thinking receives each response-required verifier's floor without calling
165	it. Set `core.reward_reasoning_mode="none"` for an explicitly non-thinking run.
166	This applies to text/code verifiers and named judges; named judges receive the
167	selected region intact, including answer tags and surrounding prose.
168	The full response and its token IDs remain available for training and recording.
169	
170	The shared `ResponseParts` object separates thinking and the delivered answer or
171	action. Trusted factory/registry declarations identify answer, process, format or
172	composite objectives. Answer objectives use `response`; explicit process/format
173	objectives may select `thinking` or `full` and separately permit a missing
174	delivered response. ToolRL declares full context for boundary format and the
175	presented response for action correctness; token-length graders retain full
176	trajectory tokens. See the [configuration, interface and
177	per-path behavior register](grading.md) before changing a run's grading policy.
178	
179	Verifiers can optionally implement
180	`async_call_final_answer(tokens, prediction, label, **kwargs)`. In final-answer
181	mode with a response view, the adapter uses this method when present; otherwise
182	it calls `async_call` with the selected string. Migrated consumers receive
183	`selected_input=True`, bypass their thinking-boundary logic and retain their
184	task-specific answer parsing. All calls run after the component's eligibility
185	and truncation gates. Response/thinking views receive empty token lists; full
186	views retain actual trajectory tokens. A structured consumer can use
187	`async_call_parts`; composites additionally receive separately selected component
188	strings. Ordinary flag-off calls retain the historical `async_call` path,
189	including any native thinking removal. Named judges use their sample-aware path.
190	
191	The built-in `R1FormatVerifier` implements this interface: after the outer gate
192	selects the final section, it checks for optional leading whitespace followed by
193	`<answer>...</answer>`, without requiring another closing-think marker. Its
194	raw-response check is unchanged. This remains a format reward, not an answer
195	correctness or content check; it retains the existing allowance for empty answer
196	tags and trailing text. In final-only mode, only the last closing marker's suffix
197	is checked, so answer tags in an earlier section cannot earn format reward.
198	
199	For native IF grading, use the built-in adapter. A complete reward registry is:
200	
201	```json
202	{
203	  "ifeval": {
204	    "factory": "open_instruct.miles.rewards.task_verifiers.ManifestIFVerifier"
205	  }
206	}
207	```
208	
209	The native adapter uses `IFEvalVerifier`, including its existing task

80	
81	Learning runs enable `training.filter_zero_std_groups=true`: constant-reward prompt
82	groups are dropped and generation replenishes the accepted training batch. Offline
83	correctness preprocessing can still be applied. The tiny `dev` mechanics
84	example explicitly disables filtering to permit all-zero-reward checks. See
85	[data and evaluation](data-and-evaluation.md#online-group-filtering) for metrics,
86	batch semantics and the opt-out.
87	
88	## Truncated responses
89	
90	The demo configs are the baseline for configuration choices unless a run explicitly
91	states otherwise. The examples use **token-mean loss weighting** and **zero reward for
92	length-truncated responses**. The Core reward default also scores truncations zero,
93	so omitting the field does not silently change the objective. The examples make
94	these choices explicit:
95	
96	```toml
97	[core]
98	reward_zero_truncated = true
99	
100	[miles]
101	calculate_per_token_loss = true
102	```
103	
104	This works with every verifier, managed judges included. It cannot be combined
105	with a `custom_reward_post_process_path` other than the default ungraded-response
106	exclusion described below. Final-answer selection and explicit verifier exceptions
107	are described in [Grading inputs and changes](grading.md).
108	
109	## Ungraded responses
110	
111	A verifier or judge request can fail for reasons unrelated to the response: a
112	code-service outage, a judge transport error, an unparseable verdict. That
113	response has no grade. Scoring it zero would place a correct answer below its
114	siblings' baseline and push the policy away from it; dropping its prompt group
115	would waste every graded sibling. By default (`core.exclude_ungraded = true`) the
116	compiler installs
117	`custom_reward_post_process_path = "open_instruct.miles.rewards.exclusion.exclude_ungraded"`:
118	the ungraded response gets zero advantage and a zeroed loss mask, its group's
119	baseline uses only the graded responses, and the paired group filter ignores it
120	when checking reward variation (groups with fewer than two graded responses are
121	dropped). The failed response keeps `metadata.reward_omission` with the verifier
122	name and error, and W&B reports `rollout/verification/ungraded_samples` and
123	`ungraded_fraction` per collection. With response-averaged loss, excluded responses
124	still count in the batch denominator, so a high failure fraction reduces the
125	policy-gradient signal per step. Groups with no trainable responses are
126	always rejected, even with `filter_zero_std_groups=false`; that setting keeps
127	valid all-zero grades, not empty groups. The collector requests replacement groups.
128	A run where every group is rejected makes no optimizer progress.
129	
130	Set `core.exclude_ungraded = false` to return to omitting the whole prompt group
131	(`rollout/verification/omitted_records`). The compiler also leaves the hook out
132	under `core.expert_balanced_packing`, which supports no reward post-process, and
133	under `miles.partial_rollout`, since the hook supports single-segment rollouts
134	only. Custom multi-segment generators must explicitly opt out as well. A custom
135	`miles.custom_convert_samples_to_train_data_path` bypasses reward postprocessing:
136	it retains group omission, and explicitly combining it with a managed exclusion
137	hook is rejected. Math verifier timeouts and code-service rejections (4xx, or a 500 that
138	persists through its retries) are not ungraded: they keep their zero reward, as
139	documented under [reward-service failure policies](data-and-evaluation.md#reward-service-failure-policies).
140	
141	For an explicitly documented overlong-filtering experiment that excludes truncated
142	responses from training instead, override the baseline with:
143	
144	```toml
145	[core]
146	reward_zero_truncated = false
147	
148	[miles]
149	custom_reward_post_process_path = "open_instruct.miles.rewards.truncation.exclude_truncated"
150	```
151	
152	Truncated responses then get zero advantage and a zeroed loss mask, and each group's
153	baseline uses only its finished, graded responses (this hook also excludes
154	ungraded responses). Raw reward metrics are unchanged. With response-averaged
155	loss, excluded responses still count in the batch denominator. When zero-variance
156	group filtering is enabled, it also considers only finished, graded responses:
157	groups with fewer than two of them or no variation in their rewards are dropped
158	before occupying training batch slots.
159	
160	## Final-answer-only rewards
161	
162	Set `core.reward_final_answer_only=true` to grade only text after the last literal
163	`</think>` by default. A missing closing marker, whitespace-only final answer or
164	reopened thinking receives each response-required verifier's floor without calling
165	it. Set `core.reward_reasoning_mode="none"` for an explicitly non-thinking run.
166	This applies to text/code verifiers and named judges; named judges receive the
167	selected region intact, including answer tags and surrounding prose.
168	The full response and its token IDs remain available for training and recording.
169	
170	The shared `ResponseParts` object separates thinking and the delivered answer or
171	action. Trusted factory/registry declarations identify answer, process, format or
172	composite objectives. Answer objectives use `response`; explicit process/format
173	objectives may select `thinking` or `full` and separately permit a missing
174	delivered response. ToolRL declares full context for boundary format and the
175	presented response for action correctness; token-length graders retain full
176	trajectory tokens. See the [configuration, interface and
177	per-path behavior register](grading.md) before changing a run's grading policy.
178	
179	Verifiers can optionally implement
180	`async_call_final_answer(tokens, prediction, label, **kwargs)`. In final-answer
181	mode with a response view, the adapter uses this method when present; otherwise
182	it calls `async_call` with the selected string. Migrated consumers receive
183	`selected_input=True`, bypass their thinking-boundary logic and retain their
184	task-specific answer parsing. All calls run after the component's eligibility
185	and truncation gates. Response/thinking views receive empty token lists; full
186	views retain actual trajectory tokens. A structured consumer can use
187	`async_call_parts`; composites additionally receive separately selected component
188	strings. Ordinary flag-off calls retain the historical `async_call` path,
189	including any native thinking removal. Named judges use their sample-aware path.
190	
191	The built-in `R1FormatVerifier` implements this interface: after the outer gate
192	selects the final section, it checks for optional leading whitespace followed by
193	`<answer>...</answer>`, without requiring another closing-think marker. Its
194	raw-response check is unchanged. This remains a format reward, not an answer
195	correctness or content check; it retains the existing allowance for empty answer
196	tags and trailing text. In final-only mode, only the last closing marker's suffix
197	is checked, so answer tags in an earlier section cannot earn format reward.
198	
199	For native IF grading, use the built-in adapter. A complete reward registry is:
200	
201	```json
202	{
203	  "ifeval": {
204	    "factory": "open_instruct.miles.rewards.task_verifiers.ManifestIFVerifier"
205	  }
206	}
207	```
208	
209	The native adapter uses `IFEvalVerifier`, including its existing task

1	# OLMo 3.5 Small (A4B) on B300
2	
3	Measured MILES RL layouts for OLMo 3.5 Small ("Hero Small", A4B,
4	`olmo35-small-e256k8-sh2x`) on `ai2/holmes` B300 nodes. Configs:
5	[two-node-mech](../../configs/miles/examples/small/two-node-mech.toml),
6	[four-node](../../configs/miles/examples/small/four-node.toml) and
7	[eight-node](../../configs/miles/examples/small/eight-node.toml). The current recipes
8	use the Tiny batch/LR/loss baseline from PR #2271; historical measurements below
9	used the earlier settings. They run four mechanics or 30 timing updates without
10	checkpoints and do not establish learning quality.
11	
12	## Model and start checkpoint
13	
14	- Start checkpoint: H203 SFT export
15	  `/weka/olmo-3p5-post-checkpoints/abhishekr/a4b-gpu/a4bgpu-s34521/hf_step18410`
16	  (`Olmo3MoeForCausalLM`, bf16, 72.58B parameters / 145.16 GB).
17	- 40 layers: 35 KDA plus full attention at layers 7, 15, 23, 31 and 39 (NoPE, head_dim 256);
18	  256 routed experts top-8 (latent MoE dim 768, `moe_intermediate_size` 3072), shared expert,
19	  dense layer 0; hidden 1536; untied LM head.
20	- Export notes: the `emo_*` fields are all null in this SFT export (the base export has
21	  EMo 8/256/256), so it is used as-is with no config edit. The HF config has
22	  `vocab_size` 100278 (LM head `[100278, 1536]`); 100352 is Core's padded size.
23	- Data: robertb's H196 Dolci inputs
24	  (`/weka/olmo-3p5-post-checkpoints/robertb/miles/h196-dolci-control-20261113/inputs/`,
25	  84,577 rendered rows). Its rendering was made for Tiny but uses the same tokenizer and chat
26	  template as this export. There is no held-out split, so do not set `training.eval_interval`.
27	- Code verifier needs `CODE_EXECUTION_TOKEN`. Each recipe maps it to a placeholder
28	  Beaker secret name under `[launch.secrets]`; replace that name with a secret in the
29	  selected workspace. Never put the token value in the TOML. The historical timing
30	  runs omitted this credential: code samples were ungraded and their groups dropped
31	  (3-36 groups per update). Runs with code grading enabled have a different effective
32	  workload; remeasure throughput rather than assuming the historical timings apply.
33	
34	## Layout and memory
35	
36	| Config | Nodes | Trainer | Engines | Judge |
37	|---|---|---|---|---|
38	| two-node-mech | 2 | 8 GPUs, EP8 | 7 × TP1 | 1 × Qwen3-32B |
39	| four-node | 4 | 8 GPUs, EP8 | 23 × TP1 | 1 × Qwen3-32B |
40	| eight-node | 8 | 16 GPUs, 2 nodes × EP8 | 47 × TP1 | 1 × Qwen3-32B |
41	
42	- Trainer (EP8, 4 nodes): peak reserved 220.5 GiB of 268.6 GiB per B300 (rank 0 peak
43	  allocated 209.7 GiB). With 2 × EP8 (8 nodes): 169.7 GiB. Packs are 34,816 tokens, below the
44	  OLMo-core no-grad Triton SwiGLU int32 overflow at 43,690 tokens per forward.
45	- Engine at R=96: weights 135 GB; KDA state for 128 slots 17.9 GB (SSM 17.64 + conv 0.21);
46	  KV for 3,342,336 tokens 63.8 GB (K 31.88 + V 31.88); about 50 GB free after pools at
47	  `mem_fraction_static` 0.88.

50	
51	- `sglang_attention_backend = "trtllm_mha"` for the 5 full-attention layers. On one engine with
52	  96 forced 4K decodes: 2,881 tok/s vs 2,473 with triton. `fa4` crashes the server: "SM100
53	  forward with head_dim=256 does not support seqused_q/seqused_k".

56	  +1.6% at R=96. The tiles only take effect in an image built with this branch's
57	  `configs/miles`; an older image has no file at that path.
58	- `OLMO_SGLANG_CORE_COMPAT = "rounding"`. The attention trial's HF vs SGLang
59	  samples have mean |Δlogprob| 0.0155-0.0223 and argmax agreement 98.2-99.4%.
60	- Admission R=96: `sglang_max_running_requests` 96, `sglang_max_mamba_cache_size` 128,
61	  `sglang_server_concurrency` 192, `sglang_cuda_graph_max_bs_decode` 96, producer budget
62	  `async_max_concurrent_samples` = 96 × engines.
63	- Judge: `timeout = 600` and `chat_template = "qwen3-no-thinking"`. The judge bindings use the
64	  hashed verifier ids in the H196 `verifiers.json`.

66	  standalone/training scoring check every update. These qualification checks add
67	  overhead relative to the original mechanics run and remain off in timing recipes
68	  (which retain the default startup scoring check).
69	- The four/eight-node recipes request 4h/3h of protected runtime, respectively,
70	  based on historical startup and update times plus headroom, with an 8h timeout.
71	  Revisit these budgets when enabling code grading or other additional work.

73	## Results
74	
75	The table below was independently recomputed from retained Beaker artifacts on
76	November 18, 2026. Updates 10-29 unless noted, 128 prompts × 8 samples, max response
77	32,768 tokens. A cycle starts at `generation_wait.started_unix` and ends at
78	`publication.started_unix + publication.seconds` for the same update. Startup,
79	final drain and checkpoint/evaluation work are excluded. Each column is its own
80	median; component medians need not sum to the cycle median. Earlier headline cycle
81	figures (299/309/399/139 seconds) were not reproduced by this definition.
82	
83	| Run | Layout | s/update (wall median) | Gen wait | Train | Publication | Engine tok/s | Notes |
84	|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
85	| [timing4](https://beaker.org/ex/01M7EWK861JCP5Z0G5514S5XJ5) | 4-node, R=96 | 276.2 (u10-24) | 109.6 | 171.2 | 8.9 | 2,528 | Failed at update 25: `/weka/oe-training-default` full |
86	| [timing4n](https://beaker.org/ex/01M7HF4C8M7XC7ZPVC9QMD8X36) | 4-node, R=96 | 301.7 | 125.7 | 174.7 | 9.1 | 2,524 | 30/30, clean exit |
87	| [timing4n-r64](https://beaker.org/ex/01M7J0V7M8VHN4X1PJ43BQ9JZQ) | 4-node, R=64 | 396.4 | 217.5 | 163.8 | 7.2 | 1,946 | 31% slower cycle median than R=96 |
88	| [timing8](https://beaker.org/ex/01M7FV0QBE1CJ2656N5DA0JYY6), u10-23 | 8-node, R=96 | 116.0 | 0.3 | 98.1 | 17.7 | 2,371 | Drains buffered work; not a steady-state topology result |
89	| timing8, u24-29 | 8-node, R=96 | 185.5 | 73.8 | 96.0 | 18.3 | — | Only six late updates; shutdown subsequently failed |
90	| [timing4n-r160](https://beaker.org/ex/01M7NHRMV28ZX4S3HXD4BWAQVJ), u10-29 | 4-node, R=160 | 182.7 | 0.3 | 163.8 | 10.0 | — | Early buffered work; 50 updates total |
91	| timing4n-r160, u30-49 | 4-node, R=160 | 248.9 | 64.8 | 173.3 | 9.8 | — | Later window; shutdown subsequently failed |

93	The engine token rates above retain the original serving summaries; cycle and stage
94	durations were audited directly. `driver_timing.jsonl`, `rollout_flow.jsonl`,
95	`pipeline_occupancy.jsonl`, `publication.jsonl`, all-rank `training_contract_rank*.jsonl`
96	and actor metric events are in each experiment's `run/checkpoints/` results.
97	The R96 and R64 runs pass `scripts/miles/analyze_throughput.py` with `warmup=10`,
98	including all eight trainer ranks and completed workflow checks. All 16 timing8
99	ranks and all eight R160 ranks completed their requested 30/50 optimizer steps,
100	respectively, without skipped updates; those experiments still failed at shutdown.
101	
102	### Topology interpretation
103	
104	- Four-node R96: trainer rollout-wait share is **35.5%** of measured driver-stage
105	  time over u10-29. R64 increases it to **54.2%**. The R96 trial delivers about
106	  30.6K useful response tokens/s versus 22.4K for R64, a 37% improvement under the
107	  strict analyzer. Publication is about 9 seconds/update and is not the largest cost.
108	- Eight-node R96: early compilation and slow trainer updates build a generation
109	  backlog. Median completed queue depth falls from 384 groups over u10-23 to zero
110	  over u24-29. Late trainer wait is **36.5%**; doubling both trainer and inference
111	  capacity did not eliminate rollout starvation. Late stale-token discard fraction
112	  is **9.3%** of delivered plus stale-discarded response tokens. Mean sample policy
113	  age has a per-update median of 8.0 versions in u10-23 and 4.9 in u24-29, versus
114	  2.2 for four-node R96. These are different operating regimes.
115	- Four-node R160: the later u30-49 window reduces wait to **24.9%**, with median
116	  sample age 3.3 versions and no stale-token discards in that window. Its early
117	  near-zero wait is not a steady-state result. This is a promising next candidate,
118	  not a qualified replacement: it failed the same final-drain boundary and has not
119	  been repeated with code grading or newer batch/loss settings.
120	- HTTP permit wait and generation-admission wait are zero at the median in these
121	  windows; unfinished work is near its configured budget. This does not isolate
122	  the judge's contribution. Rollout wait includes production, filtering and grading,
123	  and cannot be attributed entirely to policy GPU inference without more evidence.
124	- Even the successful four-node R96 run drains for 741 seconds at shutdown and
125	  leaves 29.4M completed response tokens unused (10.5% of accounted delivered plus
126	  stale-discarded plus terminal-unused tokens). Warm-cycle throughput is not a

131	longer runs with the same workload and objective, useful tokens per allocated GPU-hour,

137	from [PR #2271](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/pull/2271):

139	| Setting | Current Small baseline | Historical Small measurements |
140	|---|---|---|

145	| Group-standard-deviation normalization | Off | Off |

147	This is the starting baseline for Small; the historical throughput results do not
148	measure this combination. The serving geometry remains the submitted timing4n/timing8

152	The completed-buffer factor stays four: 1,024 prompt groups / 8,192 responses.

155	of unfinished budget plus completed-buffer capacity is therefore 4.328, 5.078 and
156	6.203 batches. Finished siblings can live outside that accounting; these figures

163	- Trainer: ~6.9K tok/s/GPU at EP8 on 4 nodes; ~6.0K tok/s/GPU with 2 × EP8; about 8.6-8.9M
164	  model tokens per update.

166	  tokens, truncation is 0-6%, and about 25% of groups are zero-std.
167	- Startup to the end of update 0: 1,953-2,429 s on 4 nodes, 1,543 s on 8 nodes.

172	  is still required. Evaluation and final HF export retain their generation-drain
173	  boundaries because they may reuse live serving resources.

176	
177	- `fa4` attention: crashes on head_dim 256 (above).
178	- R=64: slower (396 vs 302 s/update); engines gain throughput up to R=96. In single-engine
179	  forced decodes, R=144 matched R=96 and R=192 gave +19% total tok/s with each request ~40%
180	  slower.
181	- EP4 trainer: untested.
182	
183	## Code and runtime
184	
185	The original timing runs needed no Small-specific adapter or weight-sync changes. timing4 ran on image
186	01M7A0QM57N9499PGFAT73SMF0 (open-instruct a87a0feac). timing4n and r64 ran on image

189	does not use. `plan` on main resolves the timing4n config identically to 5c6645da. These
190	examples have not been run on an image built from main.
191	
192	## Qualification before a learning run
193	
194	Copy `two-node-mech.toml` to ignored `runs/`, set a fresh output path and the actual
195	workspace/secret names, then inspect `python -m open_instruct.miles plan runs/small-mech.toml`
196	and `python -m open_instruct.miles validate runs/small-mech.toml` before using the
197	[committed-image launcher](launching.md). Build the image from the revision being
198	qualified; `plan` equality cannot establish runtime equality.
199	
200	Retain the Beaker experiment link, image ID, submitted TOML and completion artifacts.
201	Verify all four updates, successful code grading, passing initial weight comparison,
202	standalone/training score agreement, publication acknowledgments and a clean exit.
203	Inspect `refresh_scores` for mixed-version responses and their historical-prefix and
204	latest-forward log-ratio diagnostics; see [Core diagnostics](core.md) and
205	[mixed-policy refresh](async-pipeline.md#mixed-policy-refresh). Those ratios include
206	policy drift and are not an isolated numerical-parity measurement.
207	
208	For publication debugging, enable `core.diagnostic_interval = 1` with
209	`miles.check_weight_update_equal = true` in the run copy to exercise the existing
210	snapshot/reset/republish checks after optimizer updates. This adds a second transfer
211	and extra gradient/update diagnostics. The check detects incomplete transfers over
212	its selected tensors; it does not independently prove the export mapping. Keep a
213	separate Core-versus-serving score comparison on identical tokens, prefixes and
214	weights as a qualification requirement. HF-versus-SGLang greedy agreement and an
215	always-zero training metric do not establish that comparison.
216	
217	Longer learning runs additionally need native checkpoint/save-resume and evaluation
218	checks. The timing recipes deliberately disable saving and have no held-out split.
219	
220	## Open items
221	
222	- R160 finished 50 updates, then failed its 900-second final generation drain.
223	  It used server concurrency 320, 192 KDA slots, CUDA graph batch 160, producer
224	  budget 3,680 and an auto-sized KV pool. Repeat after the terminal-cleanup fix
225	  and under the intended code-grading and batch/loss configuration.
226	- Judge latency is not logged per call, so the judge's share of generation wait is unmeasured.
227	- The earlier claim that `train_rollout_logprob_abs_diff` is always zero was incorrect.
228	  Raw actor metric events record about 0.008 over the measured timing windows;
229	  `collection_score_mean_abs` is about 0.0065-0.0067. These combine numerical and
230	  policy differences; they do not replace a controlled same-weight parity check.

# OLMo 3.5 Small (A4B) on B300

Measured MILES RL layouts for OLMo 3.5 Small ("Hero Small", A4B,
`olmo35-small-e256k8-sh2x`) on `ai2/holmes` B300 nodes. Configs:
[two-node-mech](../../configs/miles/examples/small/two-node-mech.toml),
[four-node](../../configs/miles/examples/small/four-node.toml) and
[eight-node](../../configs/miles/examples/small/eight-node.toml). The current recipes
use the Tiny batch/LR/loss baseline from PR #2271; historical measurements below
used the earlier settings. They run four mechanics or 30 timing updates without
checkpoints and do not establish learning quality.

## Model and start checkpoint

- Start checkpoint: H203 SFT export
  `/weka/olmo-3p5-post-checkpoints/abhishekr/a4b-gpu/a4bgpu-s34521/hf_step18410`
  (`Olmo3MoeForCausalLM`, bf16, 72.58B parameters / 145.16 GB).
- 40 layers: 35 KDA plus full attention at layers 7, 15, 23, 31 and 39 (NoPE, head_dim 256);
  256 routed experts top-8 (latent MoE dim 768, `moe_intermediate_size` 3072), shared expert,
  dense layer 0; hidden 1536; untied LM head.
- Export notes: the `emo_*` fields are all null in this SFT export (the base export has
  EMo 8/256/256), so it is used as-is with no config edit. The HF config has
  `vocab_size` 100278 (LM head `[100278, 1536]`); 100352 is Core's padded size.
- Data: robertb's H196 Dolci inputs
  (`/weka/olmo-3p5-post-checkpoints/robertb/miles/h196-dolci-control-20261113/inputs/`,
  84,577 rendered rows). Its rendering was made for Tiny but uses the same tokenizer and chat
  template as this export. There is no held-out split, so do not set `training.eval_interval`.
- Code verifier needs `CODE_EXECUTION_TOKEN`. Each recipe maps it to a placeholder
  Beaker secret name under `[launch.secrets]`; replace that name with a secret in the
  selected workspace. Never put the token value in the TOML. The historical timing
  runs omitted this credential: code samples were ungraded and their groups dropped
  (3-36 groups per update). Runs with code grading enabled have a different effective
  workload; remeasure throughput rather than assuming the historical timings apply.

## Layout and memory

| Config | Nodes | Trainer | Engines | Judge |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| two-node-mech | 2 | 8 GPUs, EP8 | 7 × TP1 | 1 × Qwen3-32B |
| four-node | 4 | 8 GPUs, EP8 | 23 × TP1 | 1 × Qwen3-32B |
| eight-node | 8 | 16 GPUs, 2 nodes × EP8 | 47 × TP1 | 1 × Qwen3-32B |

- Trainer (EP8, 4 nodes): peak reserved 220.5 GiB of 268.6 GiB per B300 (rank 0 peak
  allocated 209.7 GiB). With 2 × EP8 (8 nodes): 169.7 GiB. Packs are 34,816 tokens, below the
  OLMo-core no-grad Triton SwiGLU int32 overflow at 43,690 tokens per forward.
- Engine at R=96: weights 135 GB; KDA state for 128 slots 17.9 GB (SSM 17.64 + conv 0.21);
  KV for 3,342,336 tokens 63.8 GB (K 31.88 + V 31.88); about 50 GB free after pools at
  `mem_fraction_static` 0.88.

## Settings that matter

  96 forced 4K decodes: 2,881 tok/s vs 2,473 with triton. `fa4` crashes the server: "SM100
  forward with head_dim=256 does not support seqused_q/seqused_k".
- Tuned fused-MoE tiles (`SGLANG_MOE_CONFIG_DIR`, see
  [moe_configs](../../configs/miles/moe_configs/README.md)): kernel -9% at batch 96, decode
  +1.6% at R=96. The tiles only take effect in an image built with this branch's

- `OLMO_SGLANG_CORE_COMPAT = "rounding"`. The attention trial's HF vs SGLang

  based on historical startup and update times plus headroom, with an 8h timeout.
  Revisit these budgets when enabling code grading or other additional work.

### Recipe alignment

All three Small recipes, including mechanics, now use the Tiny learning baseline

| Setting | Current Small baseline | Historical Small measurements |
|---|---|---|
| Prompts × responses per prompt | 256 × 8 | 128 × 8 |
| Responses per optimizer update | 2,048 | 1,024 |
| Learning rate | 6e-6, constant, no warmup | 1e-6, constant, no warmup |

"""Expose the MILES workflow and inference-record tools through one command-line entry
point. The CLI loads run files and overrides for planning, validation, local
execution, Beaker submission and status queries, or dispatches record analysis and
prompt-selection commands. Runtime imports are deferred to the commands that need
them so planning remains available without the GPU stack.

Run with python -m open_instruct.miles {plan,validate,train,run,status} CONFIG.toml.

Inference-record tools use their own arguments:
python -m open_instruct.miles records summarize STORE --output DIR
python -m open_instruct.miles records select STORE --skip all_zero --output TABLE.json
"""

import argparse
import importlib
import json
import sys
from pathlib import Path

from open_instruct.miles.configuration import advisories, specs, validation
from open_instruct.miles.configuration.config import RunConfig
from open_instruct.miles.distillation import opd_config
from open_instruct.miles.errors import InputError


def main() -> None:
    if sys.argv[1:2] == ["records"]:
        module = (
            "open_instruct.miles.datasets.replay_summary"
            if sys.argv[2:3] == ["replay-pool"]
            else "open_instruct.miles.datasets.record_selection"
            if sys.argv[2:3] == ["select"]
            else "miles.utils.record_summary"
        )
        try:
            command = importlib.import_module(module)
        except ModuleNotFoundError as error:
            if error.name == "miles":
                raise SystemExit(
                    "Record analysis requires the MILES package; run it in the pinned runtime."
                ) from error
            raise
        command.main(sys.argv[3:] if sys.argv[2:3] in (["select"], ["replay-pool"]) else sys.argv[2:])
        return
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument("command", choices=("plan", "validate", "train", "run", "status"))
    parser.add_argument("config", type=Path)
    parser.add_argument(
        "--set",
        dest="overrides",
        action="append",
        default=[],
        metavar="SECTION.KEY=VALUE",
        help="Override a setting with a TOML value; repeatable, quote strings",
    )
    parser.add_argument("--debug", action="store_true", help="Show a full traceback for input errors")
    options = parser.parse_args()
    try:
        execute(parser, options)
    except InputError as error:
        if options.debug:
            raise
        parser.error(f"{options.config}: {error}")


def execute(parser, options):
    payload = validation.read_document(options.config)
    structured = "schema_version" in payload or "model" in payload
    config = (
        specs.from_dict(payload, config_path=options.config, overrides=options.overrides)
        if structured
        else RunConfig.from_dict(payload, options.overrides)
    )
    if options.command == "plan":
        planned = config.plan()
        advisories.emit(planned)
        print(json.dumps(planned, indent=2))
        return
    if options.command in ("run", "status"):
        if not structured:
            parser.error("run/status require a schema_version=1 run file; raw configs support plan/validate/train")
        launch = importlib.import_module("open_instruct.miles.execution.launch")
        if options.command == "run":
            launch.run(options.config, options.overrides)
        else:
            print(json.dumps(launch.status(config), indent=2))
        return
    if isinstance(config, opd_config.OPDRunSpec):
        if options.command == "validate":
            config.plan()
            print("OPD schema and allocation validated; runtime/model checks run in the candidate image")
        else:
            runtime = importlib.import_module("open_instruct.miles.distillation.opd_runtime")
            runtime.execute(config)
        return
    workflow = importlib.import_module("open_instruct.miles.execution.workflow")
    if options.command == "validate":
        if structured:
            planned_spec = config.plan()  # Validate physical allocation as well as trainer options.
            advisories.emit(planned_spec)
            print("Run schema, topology and MILES/Core options validated; inputs and runtime checked during train")
        else:
            workflow.parse_runtime(config)
            print("MILES arguments validated for OLMo-core")
        return
    if structured:
        workflow.execute(config)
    else:
        workflow.train_config(config)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

# MILES GRPO

MILES GRPO is the recommended path for reinforcement learning with supported
Olmo MoE models through Open Instruct, with OLMo-core training and SGLang inference.
Existing [Core/vLLM and DeepSpeed/vLLM workflows](../algorithms/grpo.md) remain
available for dense-model training. This guide covers setup, the pinned runtime
and a first run. See [support and limits](feature-parity.md) for what is available
and [development defaults](development-defaults.md) for starting settings.

## Run MILES GRPO

1. Check [model and topology support](models-and-checkpoints.md), check out the
   intended Open Instruct revision, then follow the
   [laptop/session setup](launching.md). Sibling development worktrees are unnecessary.
2. Copy [dev.toml](../../configs/miles/examples/tiny/dev.toml) to ignored
   `runs/my-grpo.toml`. Set a run name, fresh output path and compatible tiny
   checkpoint for a single-GPU colocated mechanics check. Keep barrier publication
   and offline W&B for this first exercise unless requested otherwise.
   Use [node.toml](../../configs/miles/examples/tiny/node.toml)
   for single-node math, instruction-following and code training, after preparing
   its policy, data and code-verifier service. It allocates no judge GPU.
3. Check Beaker resource access and supply credentials for the selected inputs
   and tracking mode. Run `plan` and `validate`, then inspect the rendered Beaker
   spec against the [distributed scheduling contract](launching.md#distributed-scheduling-contract);
   those commands alone do not check that contract. Set `MILES_EXISTING_IMAGE`
   to the immutable image ID and invoke
   `python -m open_instruct.miles run /path/to/run.toml` through the committed-image
   wrapper. Verify replica grouping and placement after submission.
4. Retain the launch receipt, submitted TOML and [completion artifacts](operations.md).
   Follow the run to completion and report the experiment link, image, model,
   configuration and validation outcomes.

The submitting host needs Python 3.12 and the Beaker CLI. Training runs use a
separate image built from the selected application revision and
[`runtime.lock.json`](../../runtime/miles/runtime.lock.json). Building that image

The public entrypoint is `python -m open_instruct.miles`. Its structured RunSpec
compiles into a RunConfig containing CoreConfig and native MILES options.
The Python API is available for integrations; use the structured workflow when
preparation, placement and submission should come from one file.
| Layer | Owns |
|---|---|
| Open Instruct wrapper | Config validation, preparation, verifiers, launch/receipts, run artifacts |
| MILES runtime | Rollout actors, SGLang engines, sample/advantage/loss machinery, shared transport helpers |
| Core adapter (in MILES) | Model construction, document/replay alignment, scoring/training forward, gradient synchronization, optimizer/checkpoints and tensor export |
| OLMo-core | Model and distributed-training primitives, attention/expert execution |
| olmo-sglang | Serving architecture registration and model-specific execution |
The Core actor at `miles.backends.core_utils.actor.OLMoCoreTrainRayActor` implements
the MILES trainer boundary. Its model/checkpoint code and publication machinery
live in the pinned MILES fork. The driver coordinates collections, optimization and versioned weight
publication. Dense standard-model support is isolated from the specialized MoE
path. [Implementation contracts](core.md) describe the detailed lifecycle and
[packing](sequence-packing.md) describes document/routing alignment.
[`runtime/miles/runtime.lock.json`](../../runtime/miles/runtime.lock.json) is the
source of truth for exact dependency commits and the immutable binary base.
Builds fetch those commits without patches or moving branch tips. MILES uses the
organized adapter hooks; OLMo-core provides the model, objective and checkpoint
APIs required by this adapter; olmo-sglang supplies compatible serving models.
The ordinary Open Instruct environment keeps its own dependency versions.
For a training lifecycle check, copy [dev.toml](../../configs/miles/examples/tiny/dev.toml)
to `runs/`, select a compatible tiny checkpoint, and follow the
[committed-image launcher](launching.md). Verify the rendered replica group and
retain image, config and completion artifacts. Test refresh separately when
changing publication behavior; a tiny mechanics check does not establish learning
quality.
## Adapter package layout

`open_instruct/miles/` groups code by responsibility. The public CLI remains
`python -m open_instruct.miles`; package initializers do not load the GPU runtime.

| Package | Responsibility |
|---|---|
| `configuration` | RunSpec/CoreConfig, native options, validation, topology and capacity planning |
| `execution` | Preparation, Beaker submission, cluster bootstrap and training coordination |
| MILES `backends/core_utils` | Core actor, model backends, packing, optimizer scheduling, checkpoints and trainer diagnostics |
| `rollout` | Application data-source selection and rollout metrics; managed generation, admission and completed queues live in MILES `backends/core_utils/rollout` |
| MILES `backends/core_utils/publication` | Weight delivery, engine drain, policy versions and durable policy state |
| `rewards` | Verifiers, reward routing and managed judges |
| `datasets` | Dataset preparation, mixtures, inference records and prompt selection |
| `evaluation` | Background evaluation submission, workers and result publication |
| `infrastructure` | Application artifact publication and bounded infrastructure waits; compiler/HF cache lifecycle lives in MILES |

Keep diagnostics next to the component they observe. Keep configuration imports
CPU-only, model backends loaded on demand, and package initializers minimal.
MILES `backends/core_utils/data.py` adapts samples to the trainer; `rollout/data_source.py` owns
runtime data-source behavior; `datasets/run_data.py` prepares researcher inputs.

Python integration imports use these package paths, for example
`from open_instruct.miles.configuration.run_spec import RunSpec`. The pinned
AllenAI MILES fork must use the matching trainer and rollout hook paths. Rebuild
the application image when updating this layout and its runtime pin together;
existing images retain their original code. Custom verifier factories and saved
native options must reference these package paths.
### Application callbacks and CPU tools

The backend trainer and managed rollout modules do not import Open Instruct.
Open Instruct supplies `core_records_factory` for per-question recording and
`core_evaluation_snapshot` for requested post-update HF exports. Those callbacks
preserve the existing recording and evaluation schedules. Dataset preparation,
reward callbacks, data-source selection, Beaker launch and evaluation submission
remain application-owned. The native `olmo_core` argument loader still resolves
Open Instruct's run configuration; that is an explicit configuration integration.

Small CPU planning and artifact-reader helpers remain local so `plan`, `validate`
and offline analysis work without the private runtime. Runtime integration tests
compare their algorithms with the MILES counterparts: scoring policy, capacity
reporting, timeout diagnostics, atomic JSON publication, input validation and
throughput arithmetic.

# u8-l1 MILES 总览与架构分层

## 1. 本讲目标

学完本讲，你应该能够：

1. 说出 MILES 与 `grpo.py`（Core/vLLM）、`grpo_fast.py`（DeepSpeed/vLLM）三条 RL 训练路线的关系与各自适用范围。
2. 理解 MILES 的所有权分层：open-instruct 包装层负责什么、MILES 运行时负责什么、Core 适配器经 OLMo-core 与 SGLang 又负责什么。
3. 会用 `python -m open_instruct.miles` 的五个子命令（`plan` / `validate` / `train` / `run` / `status`）以及 `records` 记录分析工具。
4. 知道维护示例按模型家族组织在 `configs/miles/examples/tiny/` 与 `configs/miles/examples/small/` 下：tiny 家族是力学/学习示例，small 家族本轮（PR #2280）从 dev 占位副本升级为实测的 OLMo 3.5 Small（A4B）B300 三档配方（two-node-mech / four-node / eight-node），且全部维护示例的损失基线已翻转为 token-mean（PR #2271）。
5. 了解文档地图的两轮扩展：上一轮新增 `grading.md` 与 `abstention.md`，本轮新增 `olmo35-small.md` 并在 `managed-judges.md` 登记未使用绑定规则。

本讲是 MILES 单元（u8）的第一篇，只做总览不深入细节；配置系统、工作流执行、奖励体系分别在 u8-l2、u8-l3、u8-l6 及之后各讲展开，Small B300 配方的显存账目与吞吐审计另立一讲（u8-l15）。

## 2. 前置知识

阅读本讲前，建议先具备以下概念（不熟悉也没关系，下面用通俗语言解释）：

- **RLVR / GRPO**：可验证奖励强化学习（RL with Verifiable Rewards）。对数学题、代码这类有标准答案的任务，可以用一个「验证器」自动判分作为奖励，而不需要训练额外的奖励模型。GRPO 是一种组相对策略优化算法：对同一个 prompt 采样一组回答，按组内奖励的相对高低计算优势。已在 u6-l1、u6-l2 讲过。
- **rollout（rollout 编排）**：RL 训练的一步是「让当前策略生成一批回答 → 判分 → 用结果更新策略」。生成这批回答的过程及其调度（队列、准入、引擎管理）称为 rollout 编排。
- **Ray actor**：Ray 分布式框架中的常驻进程，持有 GPU 资源并响应远程调用。MILES 运行时用 Ray actor 承载训练器与推理引擎。
- **OLMo-core 与 SGLang**：OLMo-core 是 Allen AI 的模型与分布式训练库（提供模型结构、checkpoint、分布式原语）；SGLang 是推理服务框架。MILES 用前者训练、后者服务。
- **TOML run 文件**：MILES 用一个结构化 TOML 文件描述一次完整运行（模型、数据、拓扑、启动、追踪等），是所有子命令的输入。
- **token-mean 与 response-mean 损失加权**：一个批次里有长有短的回答。response-mean（按响应平均）给每个回答同等权重，长回答里的每个 token 影响被稀释；token-mean（按 token 平均，`calculate_per_token_loss=true`）给每个 token 同等权重。本轮起所有维护示例统一采用 token-mean，但省略该设置时库默认仍是 response-mean，以兼容既有 run。
- **B300 与 MoE**：B300 是 NVIDIA 的 Blackwell Ultra 数据中心 GPU（AI2 的 Holmes 集群使用）；MoE（混合专家）模型每个 token 只激活部分专家参数。OLMo 3.5 Small（A4B）是 256 专家、约 0.8B 激活参数的小型 MoE 模型。
- **Beaker**：AI2 的实验平台，MILES 的 `run` 子命令把 TOML 编译成 Beaker 实验提交。不熟悉 Beaker 也不影响本讲，详见 u8-l8。

## 3. 本讲源码地图

| [docs/miles/architecture.md](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/2f7889da9248629f9415a80a45ba882544b82f1f/docs/miles/architecture.md) | 架构与开发：分层所有权表、运行时锁与镜像、启动依赖、本地开发检查、适配器包布局 |

| [docs/miles/grpo.md](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/2f7889da9248629f9415a80a45ba882544b82f1f/docs/miles/grpo.md) | MILES GRPO 指南：首次运行步骤、配置约定、判分/截断/未判分语义、发布模式 |
| [configs/miles/examples/README.md](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/2f7889da9248629f9415a80a45ba882544b82f1f/configs/miles/examples/README.md) | 维护示例的导读：按模型家族分组（tiny/small），列出六份模板的用途与基线设置 |

| [docs/miles/olmo35-small.md](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/2f7889da9248629f9415a80a45ba882544b82f1f/docs/miles/olmo35-small.md) | 本轮新增（PR #2280）：OLMo 3.5 Small B300 实测布局、显存账目、吞吐审计与失败记录 |
| [configs/miles/moe_configs/README.md](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/2f7889da9248629f9415a80a45ba882544b82f1f/configs/miles/moe_configs/README.md) | 本轮新增：SGLang fused-MoE tile 调优文件的生成、分发与版本匹配规则 |
| [docs/miles/grading.md](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/2f7889da9248629f9415a80a45ba882544b82f1f/docs/miles/grading.md) | 上一轮新增：共享判分输入（ResponseParts、objective/scope/require_response 契约）与行为变更登记 |
| [docs/miles/abstention.md](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/2f7889da9248629f9415a80a45ba882544b82f1f/docs/miles/abstention.md) | 上一轮新增：Nemotron 弃答式 QA 奖励的语义、rubric 与裁判服务复用 |

## 4. 核心概念与源码讲解

### 4.1 CLI 入口：`python -m open_instruct.miles`

#### 4.1.1 概念说明

MILES 在 open-instruct 中的公开入口只有一条命令：`python -m open_instruct.miles`。它把「规划、校验、本地执行、Beaker 提交、状态查询」以及「推理记录分析」全部收拢到一个入口后面。

为什么这样设计？

- **研究者的全部意图浓缩在一个 TOML run 文件里**。同一条命令对不同子命令复用同一份配置，避免「训练用一套脚本、提交用另一套脚本」的漂移。
- **运行时导入是延迟的**。GPU/MILES 运行时只在真正需要的子命令里才 import，因此 `plan` / `validate` 这类规划命令在没有 GPU、没有安装 MILES 私有运行时的笔记本电脑上也能运行。这一点是文档明确承诺的：[docs/miles/index.md:L21-L23](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/2f7889da9248629f9415a80a45ba882544b82f1f/docs/miles/index.md#L21-L23) 写明 "Planning does not require GPUs or mounted checkpoints"。

#### 4.1.2 核心流程

CLI 的一次执行流程：

```text
python -m open_instruct.miles COMMAND CONFIG.toml [--set SECTION.KEY=VALUE ...]
        │
        ├─ sys.argv[1] == "records"？
        │    ├─ "select"        → open_instruct.miles.datasets.record_selection
        │    ├─ "replay-pool"   → open_instruct.miles.datasets.replay_summary
        │    └─ 其他            → miles.utils.record_summary（需 MILES 运行时）
        │
        └─ 否则：argparse 解析 COMMAND ∈ {plan, validate, train, run, status}
             │
             ├─ 读取 TOML → payload
             ├─ 判断结构化：payload 含 schema_version 或 model 字段？
             │    ├─ 是 → specs.from_dict(...) 解析为 RunSpec（结构化 run 文件）
             │    └─ 否 → RunConfig.from_dict(...)（低层原始配置）
             │
             └─ 按命令分发：
                  plan     → config.plan()，打印计划 JSON + 提示（advisories）
                  validate → 结构化：plan() 全量校验；原始：parse_runtime()
                  run      → execution.launch.run()（提交 Beaker，仅限结构化）
                  status   → execution.launch.status()（仅限结构化）
                  train    → workflow.execute(config)（结构化）/ train_config（原始）
                             （OPDRunSpec 走独立的 distillation.opd_runtime 路径）
```

注意两个设计点：

1. **结构化 run 文件与低层配置双轨**。`run`/`status` 只接受 `schema_version=1` 的结构化文件；低层原始配置只支持 `plan`/`validate`/`train`。这让「研究者视角的完整 run」与「底层调参视角的 CoreConfig」都能进门，但提交必须走结构化路线。
2. **错误处理友好**。输入错误（`InputError`）默认被转成一行 `parser.error` 提示而不是一长串 traceback，加 `--debug` 才展开。

#### 4.1.3 源码精读

> 本轮三个提交（#2271/#2280/#2286）均未改动此文件，行号与上一版讲义一致。

模块 docstring 即是命令速查，明确写出五个子命令与 records 的用法：[open_instruct/miles/__main__.py:L1-L12](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/2f7889da9248629f9415a80a45ba882544b82f1f/open_instruct/miles/__main__.py#L1-L12)。其中 L4-L5 说明「运行时导入延迟到需要它的命令，规划无需 GPU 栈」这一关键约束。

`main()` 的第一步先拦截 `records` 分支，按子命令名选择实现模块；若缺 `miles` 包则给出「需在锁定运行时中运行」的退出提示：[open_instruct/miles/__main__.py:L26-L44](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/2f7889da9248629f9415a80a45ba882544b82f1f/open_instruct/miles/__main__.py#L26-L44)。这段代码同时示范了「延迟导入」模式——`importlib.import_module` 只在确定目标后才执行。

主解析器只有三个位置参数：命令、配置路径与可重复的 `--set` 覆盖：[open_instruct/miles/__main__.py:L45-L57](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/2f7889da9248629f9415a80a45ba882544b82f1f/open_instruct/miles/__main__.py#L45-L57)。L46 的 `choices=("plan", "validate", "train", "run", "status")` 就是「五个子命令」的出处。

`execute()` 读取 TOML 文档后，用 `schema_version in payload or "model" in payload` 判定结构化与否，再分别构造 `RunSpec`（经 `specs.from_dict`）或 `RunConfig`：[open_instruct/miles/__main__.py:L66-L73](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/2f7889da9248629f9415a80a45ba882544b82f1f/open_instruct/miles/__main__.py#L66-L73)。这是「TOML → RunSpec → RunConfig」编译链的入口（编译链细节在 u8-l2 精读）。

`plan` 分支调用 `config.plan()` 并打印 JSON 与 advisories，不做任何 GPU 操作：[open_instruct/miles/__main__.py:L74-L78](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/2f7889da9248629f9415a80a45ba882544b82f1f/open_instruct/miles/__main__.py#L74-L78)。

`run`/`status` 要求结构化文件并延迟导入 `execution.launch`：[open_instruct/miles/__main__.py:L79-L87](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/2f7889da9248629f9415a80a45ba882544b82f1f/open_instruct/miles/__main__.py#L79-L87)。L81 的报错信息直接写明「raw configs support plan/validate/train」。

`validate` 与 `train` 的分发：结构化校验会连物理分配一起 `plan()`，而训练交给 `workflow.execute`（细节在 u8-l3）：[open_instruct/miles/__main__.py:L96-L109](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/2f7889da9248629f9415a80a45ba882544b82f1f/open_instruct/miles/__main__.py#L96-L109)。OPD（蒸馏）规格有独立分支（L88-L95），本讲不展开。

#### 4.1.4 代码实践

**实践目标**：在无 GPU、无 MILES 运行时的机器上，用 `plan` 验证一份维护示例配置，体会「规划不需要 GPU 栈」。

**操作步骤**：

1. 在仓库根目录执行（open-instruct 用 uv 管理依赖，见 u1-l2）：

   ```bash
   uv run python -m open_instruct.miles plan configs/miles/examples/tiny/dev.toml
   ```

2. 观察输出的 JSON 计划（包含解析后的拓扑、批次几何与编译选项）以及 advisories 提示。
3. 再试一次带覆盖的规划，观察字段被就地替换：

   ```bash
   uv run python -m open_instruct.miles plan configs/miles/examples/tiny/dev.toml \
     --set training.num_rollouts=2
   ```

4. 故意打错命令名验证 argparse 的 choices 约束：

   ```bash
   uv run python -m open_instruct.miles plans configs/miles/examples/tiny/dev.toml
   ```

**需要观察的现象**：步骤 1/2 输出计划 JSON 与提示；步骤 3 中 `training.num_rollouts` 从模板里的 4 变为 2；步骤 4 报 `invalid choice` 错误并列出五个合法命令。

**预期结果**：`plan` 只做 CPU 侧的配置解析与物理分配规划，不触发 GPU 运行时导入；本讲撰写时未在本地实际执行该命令，输出样例**待本地验证**（文档承诺见 [docs/miles/index.md:L21-L23](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/2f7889da9248629f9415a80a45ba882544b82f1f/docs/miles/index.md#L21-L23)）。注意：模板中的 `/weka/.../YOUR_USERNAME/...` 是占位路径，个别校验可能对其报提示，属正常现象；`plan` 不要求挂载这些路径。

#### 4.1.5 小练习与答案

**练习 1**：为什么 `run`/`status` 拒绝低层原始配置（`RunConfig`），只接受 `schema_version=1` 的结构化文件？

**参考答案**：`run` 要把「模型、数据、拓扑、启动、挂载」完整编译成 Beaker 实验，这些信息只有结构化 RunSpec 才齐备；低层 `RunConfig` 只描述训练器参数，缺少提交所需的 launch/output 等段落。源码在 [open_instruct/miles/__main__.py:L79-L81](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/2f7889da9248629f9415a80a45ba882544b82f1f/open_instruct/miles/__main__.py#L79-L81) 显式报错。

**练习 2**：`python -m open_instruct.miles records summarize` 与 `plan` 对运行环境的依赖有何不同？

**参考答案**：`records summarize` 分发到 MILES 包内的 `miles.utils.record_summary`，需要安装 MILES 私有运行时（缺失时报「requires the MILES package」）；`plan` 只依赖 open-instruct 的 CPU 配置代码，无需 GPU 栈。见 [open_instruct/miles/__main__.py:L27-L44](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/2f7889da9248629f9415a80a45ba882544b82f1f/open_instruct/miles/__main__.py#L27-L44)。

**练习 3**：`--set name=my-run` 这样的覆盖发生在哪个阶段？与直接改 TOML 有何区别？

**参考答案**：覆盖作为 `overrides` 参数传给 `specs.from_dict` / `RunConfig.from_dict`（[open_instruct/miles/__main__.py:L69-L73](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/2f7889da9248629f9415a80a45ba882544b82f1f/open_instruct/miles/__main__.py#L69-L73)），在解析时叠加到 TOML 文档之上。区别：TOML 文件保持原样（可继续作为版本化的基准），覆盖只影响这一次调用，适合临时调参、sweep 与调试。

### 4.2 架构分层：三层所有权与适配器包布局

#### 4.2.1 概念说明

MILES 不是「又一个训练脚本」，而是把一次 RL 运行拆给三个所有者：

- **open-instruct 包装层**：研究者面对的一切——配置校验、数据准备、验证器/奖励、Beaker 提交与回执、运行产物。
- **MILES 运行时**（私有、按锁定制）：rollout actor、SGLang 推理引擎、采样/优势/损失机制、共享传输。
- **Core 适配器**（位于 MILES 内）：模型构建、打分与训练前向、梯度同步、优化器与 checkpoint、权重导出；训练走 OLMo-core，服务走 SGLang。

为什么要有这条边界？因为 open-instruct 是公开研究仓库，而 MILES 运行时（含其 pinned fork）是独立发布的私有组件。open-instruct 负责「研究者想要什么」，MILES 负责「RL 机制怎么做」，Core 适配器负责「在 OLMo-core 上真正训练」。理解这条边界后，你在 open-instruct 仓库里看到的每个 `open_instruct/miles/` 子包都能归位到某一层。

同时要记住：**MILES 不取代既有 GRPO 训练器**。`grpo.py`（Core/vLLM）与 `grpo_fast.py`（DeepSpeed/vLLM，u6-l4 讲过其 Ray 拓扑）仍是稠密模型训练与历史复现的现行选择；MILES 面向受支持的 Olmo MoE 模型（也提供稠密 Olmo 3 适配器，但验证较少）。

#### 4.2.2 核心流程

一次 MILES 运行的纵向视角：

```text
研究者编写 run.toml（schema_version=1）
        │  python -m open_instruct.miles plan / validate      ← open-instruct：CPU 校验与规划
        ▼
RunSpec ──编译──▶ RunConfig（含 CoreConfig 与原生 MILES 选项）
        │  python -m open_instruct.miles run                  ← open-instruct：编译 Beaker 实验并提交
        ▼
Beaker 上的应用镜像（按 runtime/miles/runtime.lock.json 构建）
        │
        ▼
MILES 运行时启动：Ray 集群、裁判加载、工作流准备并发启动
        │
        ▼
Core 适配器（OLMoCoreTrainRayActor）：SGLang 服务策略 → rollout → 打分 →
OLMo-core 训练前向/反向 → 权重发布（refresh/barrier/engine_drain）→ checkpoint/导出
```

分层所有权表（五层，前三层是所有权划分，后两层是上游基座）：

| 层 | 拥有 |
|---|---|
| Open Instruct 包装层 | 配置校验、准备、验证器、提交/回执、运行产物 |
| MILES 运行时 | rollout actor、SGLang 引擎、采样/优势/损失机制、共享传输助手 |
| Core 适配器（在 MILES 中） | 模型构建、文档/回放对齐、打分与训练前向、梯度同步、优化器/checkpoint、张量导出 |
| OLMo-core | 模型与分布式训练原语、注意力/专家执行 |
| olmo-sglang | 服务架构注册与模型专属执行 |

**练习 2**：如果要在 MILES 训练中新增一种自定义验证器，改动应落在哪一层？为什么？

**参考答案**：落在 open-instruct 包装层的 `open_instruct/miles/rewards/`（验证器、奖励路由与托管裁判），以可信注册表条目（factory + 配置）暴露给 MILES。因为后端训练器与托管 rollout 模块不导入 open-instruct（[docs/miles/architecture.md:L304-L313](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/2f7889da9248629f9415a80a45ba882544b82f1f/docs/miles/architecture.md#L304-L313)），MILES 侧只通过约定路径消费应用侧回调与注册表。（验证器细节见 u8-l6。）

**练习 3**：为什么 open-instruct 的普通 `uv.lock` 环境跑不了 MILES 训练，而 `plan` 却能跑？

**参考答案**：训练需要 MILES 私有运行时、SGLang 与锁定版本的 OLMo-core，这些由 `runtime/miles/runtime.lock.json` 与专用应用镜像提供（[docs/miles/architecture.md:L25-L30](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/2f7889da9248629f9415a80a45ba882544b82f1f/docs/miles/architecture.md#L25-L30)、[docs/miles/architecture.md:L179-L193](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/2f7889da9248629f9415a80a45ba882544b82f1f/docs/miles/architecture.md#L179-L193)）；`plan` 只走 CPU 配置代码，CLI 把运行时 import 延迟到需要它的命令（[open_instruct/miles/__main__.py:L4-L5](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/2f7889da9248629f9415a80a45ba882544b82f1f/open_instruct/miles/__main__.py#L4-L5)）。

#### 4.3.5 小练习与答案

**练习 1**：想在本地修改 `docs/miles/configuration.md` 中的一个字段默认值，直接编辑该文件对吗？

**参考答案**：不对。`configuration.md` 等生成式参考页由 MkDocs 从配置源在内存中生成、不入库；应编辑源定义与审校描述，再用 `python -m scripts.miles.generate_docs` 重新生成、`--check` 校验。见 [docs/miles/index.md:L55-L63](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/2f7889da9248629f9415a80a45ba882544b82f1f/docs/miles/index.md#L55-L63)。
